﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229X — norm-ten ramified division closure via physical genus-seven receivers


STATUS: POST_229W_NORM10_RAMIFIED_DIVISION_CLOSED / PROVED_COPRIME_RAMIFIED_PULLBACK / PROVED_PHYSICAL_GAUSSIAN_SQUARE_FORCES_PREIMAGE_X_SQUARE / PROVED_TWO_FIXED_SMOOTH_GENUS7_RECEIVERS / FALTINGS_GIVES_FINITE_NORM10_PARAMETER_AND_TWIST_SUPPORT / PROVED_NORM10_DEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_COUNT_Bo1 / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229W NORM10_RAMIFIED_DIVISION_GATE / EXACT CM COPRIME PULLBACK / PHYSICAL BASE-NORM RESTORATION / FIXED HYPERELLIPTIC RECEIVERS / SUBGATE CLOSURE


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229W
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229V reduced primitive norm-ten CM dependence to
  [1-i]P=[beta]R',    N(beta)=5,    R' in E_d(Q),
with
  r=X(R')/d=epsilon*d*t^2,
and showed that the residual rational carrier is genus zero:
  w^2=epsilon(q^2-1),    q=d*t^2.
229V correctly concluded that the raw squareclass carrier alone does not support the direct 229U genus>1 argument.


This card restores the physical conditions that 229V deliberately had not yet used: X(P)/d is a square in K=Q(i), and its Gaussian square root p satisfies N(p) in Q^{*2}. Those conditions lift the two genus-zero sign branches to two fixed smooth genus-seven curves. Faltings plus retained 229L then closes the entire norm-ten dependence branch at B^{o(1)}.


No global Stage37 gate is closed.


2. Coprime pullback through [1-i]


Fix the representative
  beta=2-i,    N(beta)=5.
All primitive norm-ten slopes are obtained from the corresponding alpha=(1+i)beta by units and conjugation; the physical norm-square packet is invariant under those finite operations up to swapping the + and - selectors.


Retain 229V:
  [1-i]P=[beta]R'.                                  (229X.1)


Because beta and 1-i are coprime in Z[i], choose A,B in Z[i] with
  A*beta+B*(1-i)=1.
Define
  Q=[A]P+[B]R'.
Then, using (229X.1),
  [1-i]Q
   =[A][1-i]P+[B][1-i]R'
   =[A beta+B(1-i)]R'
   =R'.                                             (229X.2)


Moreover
  [1-i](P-[beta]Q)=0,
so
  P=[beta]Q+S,    S in ker[1-i]={O,T0}, T0=(0,0).   (229X.3)


The T0 translate is harmless for the physical square conditions: on normalized x it sends z to -1/z. Since -1=i^2 is a K-square, z is a K-square iff -1/z is; and N of a Gaussian square root is inverted, so being a rational square is preserved. Likewise N(z+1) and N(z-1) are swapped up to division by N(z), preserving their square status on the physical packet.


Thus it suffices to analyze S=O.


RESULT_229X_COPRIME_RAMIFIED_PULLBACK=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Exact normalized coordinates


Write
  z=X(Q)/d in K,
  r=X(R')/d in Q.


The exact [1-i] x-map retained in 229V gives
  r=i(z^2-1)/(2z).                                 (229X.4)


For beta=2-i, the norm-five map is the conjugate of 229T:
  X([beta]Q)/d = z H_beta(z)^2,                    (229X.5)
where
  H_beta(z)
   = ((2+i)z^2-i)(z^2-1-2i)/(5z^4-2z^2+1).       (229X.6)


A positive physical endpoint has
  X(P)/d=p^2,    p in K^*,
  N(p) in Q^{*2}.                                 (229X.7)


By (229X.3)-(229X.5), away from the already excluded torsion/pole boundaries, (229X.7) implies z is a K-square. Write z=s^2. Then one may take p=s H_beta(z), up to the harmless T0 reciprocal. Therefore the base norm condition is exactly
  N(s) N(H_beta(z)) in Q^{*2}.                    (229X.8)


This is the physical condition that was not used in the genus-zero firewall of 229V.


RESULT_229X_PHYSICAL_GAUSSIAN_SQUARE_FORCES_Q_X_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229X_BASE_NORM_CONDITION_AFTER_PULLBACK=PROVED_EXACT.


4. epsilon=+1 branch gives a fixed genus-seven receiver


Put
  r=q=d t^2>0.
The rational E_d equation from 229V gives
  w^2=q^2-1.                                      (229X.9)


Solving (229X.4),
  z=i h,
with
  h=-q+w  or  h=-q-w,
and the two h-values are reciprocal. Since q>|w| on the nonboundary real branch, h<0.


Because z=i h is a K-square, there is a in Q^* with
  h=-2a^2,                                        (229X.10)
indeed (a(1-i))^2=-2i a^2.


For z=i h, exact multiplication of (229X.6) by its conjugate gives
  N(H_beta(i h))
    =(h^4+2h^2+5)/(5h^4+2h^2+1).                (229X.11)


With s=a(1-i), N(s)=2a^2. Thus (229X.8) is equivalent to
  2*(16a^8+8a^4+5)/(80a^8+8a^4+1)
being a rational square. Equivalently every physical point on this sign branch maps to the fixed curve


  C_+:
  Y^2=2 A_+(a) B_+(a),                           (229X.12)


  A_+(a)=16a^8+8a^4+5,
  B_+(a)=80a^8+8a^4+1.


Exact polynomial arithmetic gives
  Disc(A_+)=Disc(B_+)=2^60*5^3,
  Res(A_+,B_+)=2^68.                              (229X.13)


Hence A_+ and B_+ are squarefree and coprime. The right side of (229X.12) is squarefree of degree 16, so the smooth projective model C_+ has genus
  g=(16-2)/2=7.                                   (229X.14)


RESULT_229X_NORM10_PLUS_BRANCH_FIXED_CURVE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229X_NORM10_PLUS_BRANCH_GENUS=7.


5. epsilon=-1 branch gives a second fixed genus-seven receiver


Put
  r=-q,    q=d t^2>0.
The residual conic is
  w^2=1-q^2.                                      (229X.15)


Solving (229X.4) gives
  z=w+i q
or its reciprocal/conjugate variant; in particular
  N(z)=1.


Since z=s^2 and N(z)=1, N(s)=1. Every rational norm-one s is parameterized, up to the usual finite boundary points, by
  s=(u-i)/(u+i),    u in Q.
Therefore
  z=((u-i)/(u+i))^2.                              (229X.16)


Substituting (229X.16) into (229X.6) and taking the exact K/Q norm gives


  N(H_beta(z))=C(u)/D(u),                         (229X.17)


where
  C(u)=u^8+8u^7+20u^6-56u^5-26u^4+56u^3+20u^2-8u+1,
  D(u)=u^8-8u^7+20u^6+56u^5-26u^4-56u^3+20u^2+8u+1.


Since N(s)=1, the physical base condition (229X.8) is equivalent to C(u)/D(u) being a rational square, hence to the fixed curve


  C_-:
  Y^2=C(u)D(u).                                   (229X.18)


Exact polynomial arithmetic gives
  Disc(C)=Disc(D)=2^60*5^3,
  Res(C,D)=2^68.                                  (229X.19)


Thus C and D are squarefree and coprime. Their product is squarefree of degree 16, so the smooth projective model C_- also has genus 7.


RESULT_229X_NORM10_MINUS_BRANCH_FIXED_CURVE=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229X_NORM10_MINUS_BRANCH_GENUS=7.


6. Faltings closes norm-ten parameter and twist support


Retain the Faltings theorem input already accepted in 229U/229W: a smooth projective curve of genus >1 over Q has finitely many Q-rational points.


By Sections 4-5,
  C_+(Q) and C_-(Q)
are finite. Therefore only finitely many rational parameters a or u occur in physical norm-ten dependence.


For the + branch, h determines
  q=-(h+h^{-1})/2.
For the - branch, u determines q through (229X.16), equivalently
  q=-4u(u^2-1)/(u^2+1)^2
up to the harmless conjugate/orientation choice.


In either branch q=d t^2 with canonical positive squarefree d. Hence each surviving rational parameter fixes one canonical twist class d. Therefore norm-ten dependence realizes only finitely many d.


Retain 229L: for every fixed canonical d, the number of positive physical endpoints of physical height R_phys<=B mapping to E_d is uniformly B^{o(1)}.


The number of unit/conjugate norm-ten slopes and the T0 translate are absolute constants. Consequently


  #{positive physical endpoints R_phys<=B
      in CM dependence with N(alpha)=10}
    =B^{o(1)}
    =o(B^{1/3}).                                  (229X.20)


RESULT_229X_NORM10_PARAMETER_SUPPORT=FINITE_BY_FALTINGS.
RESULT_229X_NORM10_REALIZED_TWIST_SUPPORT=FINITE.
RESULT_229X_NORM10_DEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_COUNT=B^{o(1)}.
RESULT_229X_NORM10_BRANCH=CLOSED_FOR_STAGE37_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET.


7. Relation to 229V and updated dependence status


229V is not retracted. Its genus-zero statement is correct for the raw squareclass carrier r=±d t^2. What changes is that the exact physical ramified-division pullback adds the K-square condition on X(Q)/d and the rational-square condition on N(p). Those conditions cut the two raw conics by fixed genus-seven receivers.


Updated CM dependence status:
- norm2: physically empty by 229S;
- norm5: B^{o(1)}, closed by 229U;
- norm10: B^{o(1)}, CLOSED by 229X;
- all odd norms: preimages rationalized by 229W;
- norm13: B^{o(1)}, closed by 229W;
- remaining bounded odd norms >=17: fixed alpha-dependent base-selector curves still to audit;
- remaining even norms >10: parity-aware bounded-image analysis remains open.


This is subgate counting credit only. It does not alter the whole-endpoint preferred gate.


8. Global route status


CURRENT_PREFERRED_GATE remains
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(e R_phys, x y))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


Useful next inputs:
(A) next unresolved bounded CM dependence norm, with odd norm17 now cleaner than norm10;
(B) a uniform theorem closing all remaining bounded CM slopes;
(C) selector-conditioned twist/radical-support theorem that attacks the preferred whole-population gate directly.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


9. Verification scope


Within-session exact symbolic verification:
- (229X.11) checked by exact conjugate multiplication.
- For A_+,B_+: Disc=2^60*5^3 for each and resultant=2^68.
- For C,D: Disc=2^60*5^3 for each and resultant=2^68.
- C_+ and C_- therefore have squarefree degree-16 branch polynomials and genus 7.
- The norm-one parametrization in (229X.16) satisfies w^2+q^2=1 identically.


This is not an independent hostile audit. Integrated audit186–229O remains unchanged in scope and is not silently extended to 229P–X.


10. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229W;
- 229V norm10 ramified reduction;
- 229T norm5 exact CM x-map;
- 229L physical Gaussian twist router and fixed-d B^{o(1)} fiber;
- 229J physical norm-square selector packet;
- current MAIN / CARD-INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE.


External theorem:
- no new theorem species. Faltings is reused only through the already accepted 229U/229W input.


FINAL_READBACK_RECEIPT: PASS. Card, CARD-INDEX row489, 案内 latest/read-order, RESULT-LEDGER, MAIN current override, and active ROUTE were read back from Drive and agree on 229X. Norm10 is closed only for the Stage37 one-third CM-dependence budget at B^o(1); preferred whole-population radical-gcd gate remains OPEN, GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0, M3-T11-230 unissued, production HOLD retained. Integrated audit186–229O scope unchanged.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229W — all odd-norm rationalization and norm-thirteen genus-eleven closure


STATUS: POST_229V_ALL_ODD_NORM_RATIONALIZATION_COMPLETE / PROVED_ODD_CM_X_RATIO_IS_SQUARE / PROVED_ALL_ODD_DEPENDENCE_PREIMAGES_RATIONAL / PROVED_ALL_ODD_DEPENDENCE_REDUCES_TO_RATIONAL_QUARTIC_CARRIERS / PROVED_NORM13_FIXED_SMOOTH_GENUS11_RECEIVER / FALTINGS_GIVES_FINITE_NORM13_SUPPORT / PROVED_NORM13_DEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_COUNT_Bo1 / NORM10_REMAINS_OPEN / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN


TYPE: POST-229V ODD-NORM UNIFICATION / DIVISOR-THEORETIC CM SQUARE FACTOR / 2-ADIC COCYCLE ELIMINATION / NORM13 FIXED HYPERELLIPTIC RECEIVER / SUBGATE CLOSURE


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229V
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229T proved for odd norm that dependence admits an alpha-preimage Q with
  P=[alpha]Q,
  2Q in E_d(Q),
and proved for norm5 by explicit formula that x([alpha]Q)/x(Q) is a square, forcing Q itself to be rational after a 2-adic cocycle audit.


229U then closed norm5 at B^o(1).
229V showed that norm10 is different because the ramified factor 1+i leaves a genus-zero residual carrier.


This card proves that the norm5 square-factor/rationalization phenomenon is not special to norm5: it holds for EVERY Gaussian alpha of odd norm. It then applies this general result to the next odd primitive norm 13 and closes that entire dependence branch at B^o(1) through an explicit fixed genus-11 curve.


No global Stage37 gate is closed.


2. General odd-norm CM square-factor theorem


Let
  K=Q(i),
  E_d:Y^2=X^3-d^2X,
  T0=(0,0),
and let
  phi=[alpha], alpha=a+bi in Z[i],
with N(alpha) odd.


The divisor of X on E_d is
  div(X)=2(T0)-2(O).                             (229W.1)


Consider
  F_alpha = (X composed with [alpha])/X in K(E_d)^*.
Then
  div(F_alpha)
   =2D_alpha,
where
  D_alpha=[alpha]^*(T0-O)-(T0-O).               (229W.2)


Under Pic^0(E_d)≅E_d and the principal polarization, pullback by [alpha] acts as the dual endomorphism [bar(alpha)]. Hence
  [D_alpha]=[bar(alpha)]T0-T0.                   (229W.3)


Now [i] fixes T0. Since N(alpha)=a^2+b^2 is odd, a and b have opposite parity, so a-b is odd. Therefore
  [bar(alpha)]T0=[a-bi]T0=(a-b)T0=T0.
Thus
  [D_alpha]=0.


Hence D_alpha is principal over K. Choose h_alpha in K(E_d)^* with
  div(h_alpha)=D_alpha
and normalize h_alpha(O)=1.


Using the standard formal parameter at O, the differential of [alpha] is multiplication by alpha, so
  F_alpha(O)=alpha^(-2).
Therefore
  F_alpha=(h_alpha/alpha)^2.                    (229W.4)


Equivalently, for every nonexceptional Q,
  X([alpha]Q)/X(Q) is a square in K.             (229W.5)


RESULT_229W_ODD_CM_X_RATIO_IS_K_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


This proof is intrinsic and does not require an explicit division polynomial.


3. All odd-norm dependence preimages are rational


Take a physical dependent endpoint with primitive odd-norm alpha. Retain 229T:
  P=[alpha]Q,
  2Q in E_d(Q).                                  (229W.6)


Write
  r=X(Q)/d,
  X(P)/d=p^2.


By (229W.5),
  X(P)/d = r * h^2
for some h in K^* at Q. Since the left side is the physical K-square p^2,
  r is a square in K:
  r=s^2.                                         (229W.7)


Because 2Q is rational,
  sigma(Q)=Q+S,
  S in E[2].
Retain the exact 2-torsion translation packet from 229T:
  S=O:   bar(r)=r;
  S=T0:  bar(r)=-1/r;
  S=T+:  bar(r)=(r+1)/(r-1);
  S=T-:  bar(r)=(1-r)/(1+r).                    (229W.8)


If S=T0 then N(r)=-1, impossible for r=s^2.


If S=T+ then N(r-1)=2.
If S=T- then N(r+1)=2.
The 229T (1+i)-adic lemma gives, for every s in K,
  v_(1+i)(s^2 plus/minus 1) != 1,
hence
  N(s^2 plus/minus 1) !=2.


Therefore S=O and
  Q in E_d(Q).                                   (229W.9)


RESULT_229W_ALL_ODD_NORM_CM_PREIMAGES_RATIONAL=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Universal rational quartic carrier for odd dependence


Now
  r in Q
and r=s^2 in K.
A rational K-square is plus or minus a rational square, so
  r=epsilon t^2,
  epsilon in {+1,-1},
  t in Q^*.                                      (229W.10)


Write Q=(d r,y_Q). The curve equation yields
  (y_Q/(dt))^2 = d(t^4-1)       for epsilon=+1,
  (y_Q/(dt))^2 = d(1-t^4)       for epsilon=-1.  (229W.11)


Thus EVERY odd-norm dependence branch lies over the same two rational quartic twist carriers
  W^2=d(t^4-1),
  W^2=d(1-t^4),                                  (229W.12)
with the alpha-dependent physical pullback condition
  P=[alpha]Q
and the retained 229J selector conditions.


RESULT_229W_ALL_ODD_DEPENDENCE_REDUCES_TO_RATIONAL_QUARTIC_CARRIERS=PROVED_EXACT.


This does not itself count the odd branches; the alpha-dependent base selector remains decisive.


5. Norm13 explicit CM map


The next primitive odd norm after the already-closed norm5 is 13. Up to unit and conjugation take
  alpha=3+2i.


On normalized coordinate
  r=X(Q)/d,
direct exact addition on E_d gives


  X([3+2i]Q)/d
    = -r * (A(r)/B(r))^2
    = r * H_13(r)^2,                             (229W.13)


where
  A(r)=r^6+(-11+10i)r^4+(7-4i)r^2+(3+2i),


  B(r)=(2-3i)r^6+(-4-7i)r^4+(10+11i)r^2-i,


and
  H_13(r)=i A(r)/B(r).                           (229W.14)


The unit factor i has norm 1.


All primitive norm13 Gaussian slopes are associates/conjugates of 3+2i. Unit multiplication changes normalized X only by a sign and conjugation conjugates the formula, so the rational norm condition below is the same for the entire norm13 packet.


RESULT_229W_NORM13_EXACT_CM_X_MAP=PROVED_EXACT.


6. The physical base selector becomes a fixed genus-11 curve


By Sections 3-4, Q is rational and
  r=epsilon t^2.


Choose eta in {1,i} with eta^2=epsilon. From (229W.13),
  p=plus/minus eta*t*H_13(r).
Hence
  N(p)=t^2 * N(H_13(r)).                         (229W.15)


The physical 229J base condition
  N(p) in Q^{*2}
is therefore equivalent to
  N(H_13(r)) in Q^{*2}.                          (229W.16)


Exact multiplication gives
  N(H_13(r))=A_13(r)/B_13(r),                    (229W.17)
where


  A_13(r)
   =r^12-22r^10+235r^8-228r^6
     +39r^4+26r^2+13,


  B_13(r)
   =13r^12+26r^10+39r^8-228r^6
     +235r^4-22r^2+1.                            (229W.18)


Therefore every physical norm13 dependent endpoint yields a rational point on the fixed curve


  C_13:
  U^2=A_13(r)B_13(r).                            (229W.19)


The physical non-torsion locus avoids A_13 B_13=0/poles, so no endpoint boundary correction is created here.


RESULT_229W_NORM13_BASE_SELECTOR_TO_FIXED_CURVE=PROVED_EXACT.


7. C_13 is smooth of genus 11


Exact polynomial calculations give


  Disc(A_13)=2^132 * 13^5 !=0,
  Disc(B_13)=2^132 * 13^5 !=0,
  Res(A_13,B_13)=2^150 !=0.                     (229W.20)


Thus A_13 and B_13 are individually squarefree and coprime.
Their product is squarefree of degree 24.


Hence the smooth projective model of C_13 is hyperelliptic of genus
  g=(24-2)/2=11.                                 (229W.21)


RESULT_229W_NORM13_FIXED_CURVE_SMOOTH=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229W_NORM13_FIXED_CURVE_GENUS=11.


8. Faltings closes the norm13 r-support


Retain the Faltings theorem input already used and audited in 229U:
a smooth projective curve of genus greater than 1 over Q has finitely many Q-rational points.


Since C_13 has genus 11,
  C_13(Q) is finite.                             (229W.22)


Therefore only finitely many rational r can occur in physical norm13 dependence.


RESULT_229W_NORM13_RATIONAL_r_SUPPORT=FINITE_BY_FALTINGS.


No effective enumeration of C_13(Q) is claimed or needed.


9. Finite r implies finite norm13 twist support and B^o(1) endpoint count


For rational Q=(dr,y_Q),
  (y_Q/d)^2=d*r*(r^2-1).
Therefore
  [d]=[r(r^2-1)]
in Q^*/Q^{*2}.                                   (229W.23)


Each surviving rational r fixes at most one canonical positive squarefree twist d. Hence norm13 dependence realizes only finitely many canonical twists.


Retain 229L:
for every fixed canonical d, the number of positive physical endpoints with R_phys<=B mapping to E_d is uniformly B^o(1).


Consequently


  #{positive physical endpoints R_phys<=B
      in CM dependence with N(alpha)=13}
    =B^o(1)
    =o(B^(1/3)).                                 (229W.24)


RESULT_229W_NORM13_REALIZED_TWIST_SUPPORT=FINITE.
RESULT_229W_NORM13_DEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_COUNT=B^{o(1)}.
RESULT_229W_NORM13_BRANCH=CLOSED_FOR_STAGE37_ONE_THIRD_BUDGET.


This is subgate counting credit only.


10. Updated CM dependence status


- norm2: physically empty by 229S;
- norm5: B^o(1), closed by 229U;
- norm10: exact ramified-prime/genus-zero reduction by 229V, COUNT OPEN;
- ALL odd norms: preimage rationalization and universal quartic reduction proved by 229W;
- norm13: B^o(1), closed by 229W;
- remaining bounded odd norms >=17: no cocycle work is needed; attack only the fixed alpha-dependent base-selector curve;
- remaining even norms: retain 229S/229V parity-aware bounded-image analysis.


The next odd target is norm17, not a repetition of the norm5 cocycle calculation.


11. Global route status


The preferred whole-endpoint gate remains unchanged:


  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(eR_phys,xy))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


Useful next inputs:
(A) direct same-physical control of NORM10_RAMIFIED_DIVISION_GATE;
(B) norm17 fixed base-selector curve audit using the new all-odd rationalization;
(C) a uniform theorem covering the finitely many remaining odd alpha at once;
(D) selector-conditioned support or direct radical-support theorem.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


12. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229V;
- 229U norm5 fixed-genus3/Faltings closure;
- 229T odd-norm pullback and 2-adic cocycle lemma;
- 229S bounded Gaussian dependence slopes;
- 229L fixed-d B^o(1) fiber and Hilbert-90 twist adapter;

229U closed the norm-five CM-dependence branch at B^o(1). The smallest remaining primitive Gaussian norm is 10, represented up to unit/conjugation by
  alpha=3+i=(1+i)(2-i).


This card gives the exact norm-ten parity reduction and proves that the easy 229U genus>1/Faltings mechanism does NOT transfer: after the forced squareclass reduction, the residual necessary carrier is genus zero.


No endpoint saving is claimed.


2. Exact norm-ten factorization and torsion absorption


Retain 229S:
  2P=[alpha]R+T,
  R in E_d(Q) non-torsion,
  T in E[2],
for a dependent physical point.


Write
  alpha=(1+i) beta,
  N(beta)=5.


Multiply by 1-i:
  2[1-i]P=2[beta]R+[1-i]T.


Set
  X=[1-i]P-[beta]R.
Then

Hence X is K-torsion. Retain 229Q:
  E_d(Q(i))_tors=E[2]
for physical squarefree d>1.
Therefore [2]X=0, so necessarily
  [1-i]T=0,
and
  X=S in E[2].


Thus the original torsion term is restricted to ker[1-i]={O,(0,0)}.


Because N(beta)=5 is odd, [beta] is bijective on E[2]. Choose S' in E[2] with

Retain the 229L Hilbert-90 selector squareclasses:
  z+1=delta_+ a_+^2,
  z-1=delta_- a_-^2,

  [d]=[delta_+ delta_-]
in Q^*/Q^{*2}, up to the retained harmless sign kernel into Q(i).

  i/2=((1+i)/2)^2
is a square in Q(i), and z=p^2 is a square, (229V.2) yields
  [s]=[delta_+ delta_-]=[d]
in Q(i)^*/Q(i)^{*2}.                             (229V.3)


On the other hand, (229V.1) is a norm-five CM map from the rational point R'. Put
  r=x(R')/d in Q.
Retain the 229T norm-five form

in Q(i)^*/Q(i)^{*2}.                             (229V.4)

in Q(i)^*/Q(i)^{*2}.                             (229V.5)

  Q^*/Q^{*2} -> Q(i)^*/Q(i)^{*2}

such that

  y_R^2
   =epsilon*d^4*t^2*(d^2 t^4-1).

  w^2=epsilon(q^2-1).                            (229V.7)


Thus the two sign branches are


  epsilon=+1:

  epsilon=-1:
    q^2+w^2=1.                                   (229V.8)


Both are rational conics, hence genus zero, with infinite rational parametrizations.


RESULT_229V_NORM10_RESIDUAL_DESCENT_CARRIER=GENUS_ZERO_EXACT.


This is a NO-GO result for the immediate reuse of 229U:
the surviving norm-ten squareclass condition does not produce a fixed genus>1 curve to which Faltings can be applied.

    [1-i]P=[beta]R',

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229U — norm-five selector saturation and fixed genus-three finiteness


STATUS: POST_229T_NORM5_GATE_CLOSED_UP_TO_Bo1 / PROVED_NORM5_ENDPOINT_SELECTORS_AUTOMATIC_EXCEPT_BASE_NORM / PROVED_BASE_NORM_REDUCES_TO_FIXED_SMOOTH_GENUS3_CURVE / FALTINGS_GIVES_FINITE_RATIONAL_r / PROVED_NORM5_REALIZED_TWIST_SUPPORT_FINITE / PROVED_NORM5_DEPENDENT_ENDPOINT_COUNT_Bo1 / GLOBAL_GATE_UNCHANGED / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0 / NO_REOPEN

PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN

GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229T reduced every physical norm-five dependence point to
  P=[alpha]Q,
  Q in E_d(Q),
  alpha of Gaussian norm 5,
with
  r:=x(Q)/d = epsilon t^2,
  epsilon in {+1,-1},
  t in Q^*,
and the rational quartic carrier
  W^2=d(t^4-1)        for epsilon=+1,
or
  W^2=d(1-t^4)        for epsilon=-1.


The remaining question was whether the retained 229J physical selector conditions cut this genus-one carrier enough to give a same-physical bound.


This card proves that the two endpoint selectors N(p^2 plus/minus 1) become AUTOMATIC squares on the norm-five CM image, while the base condition N(p) square cuts the carrier by one fixed smooth genus-three curve independent of d. Faltings then makes the rational r-support finite. Combined with 229L fixed-d fiber B^o(1), the entire norm-five dependent endpoint contribution is B^o(1).


This is genuine subgate counting credit only. It does not prove the global Stage37 gate.


2. Exact norm-five Lattes coordinate


Take alpha=2+i. Retain 229T:
  p^2 = x(P)/d = F(r)=r H(r)^2,
where
  H(r)=(((2-i)r^2+i)(r^2-1+2i))
       /(5r^4-2r^2+1).                          (229U.1)


Set
  D(r)=5r^4-2r^2+1,
  A(r)=r^4-2r^2+5.                              (229U.2)


For real rational r,
  H(r) conjugate(H(r)) = A(r)/D(r).             (229U.3)


The other norm-five slopes are obtained from 2+i by conjugation, sign, or multiplication by the unit i. Conjugation leaves all norms below unchanged; sign leaves x unchanged; multiplication by i changes F to -F and swaps the plus/minus endpoint selectors. Hence it is enough to compute for alpha=2+i.


RESULT_229U_NORM5_NORM_FACTOR=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Endpoint selector saturation: N(p^2 plus/minus 1) are automatic squares


A direct exact factorization gives


  N(F(r)+1)
   = [
       (r-1)(r^4+4r^3+10r^2+4r+1)
       /D(r)
     ]^2,                                        (229U.4)


  N(F(r)-1)
   = [
       (r+1)(r^4-4r^3+10r^2-4r+1)
       /D(r)
     ]^2.                                        (229U.5)


Therefore for every rational r at which the non-torsion norm-five map is defined,
  N(p^2+1) in Q^{*2},
  N(p^2-1) in Q^{*2}
hold identically.


Thus the two endpoint selectors that were nontrivial on the ambient 229J torus give NO further arithmetic thinning on the norm-five rational CM carrier.


RESULT_229U_NORM5_ENDPOINT_PLUS_SELECTOR=AUTOMATIC_SQUARE.
RESULT_229U_NORM5_ENDPOINT_MINUS_SELECTOR=AUTOMATIC_SQUARE.
RESULT_229U_NORM5_ENDPOINT_SELECTOR_SATURATION=PROVED_EXACT.


This is an important firewall: norm-five dependence cannot be disposed by reusing only the two endpoint norm-square tests.


4. The base norm condition is the surviving selector


229J also requires
  N(p) in Q^{*2}.


Since r=epsilon t^2 and p is a square root of F=rH^2, one may take
  p=tH(r)          when epsilon=+1,
  p=i t H(r)       when epsilon=-1,
up to the harmless sign.


In either case
  N(p)=t^2 A(r)/D(r).                            (229U.6)


Because t^2 is already a rational square, the physical base condition is equivalent to
  A(r)/D(r) in Q^{*2}.                           (229U.7)


Equivalently, with U in Q,
  C_5:
  U^2=A(r)D(r)
     =(r^4-2r^2+5)(5r^4-2r^2+1).               (229U.8)


RESULT_229U_NORM5_BASE_SELECTOR_EQUIVALENT_TO_FIXED_CURVE=PROVED_EXACT.


Crucially, C_5 is independent of d, B, alpha, and the endpoint packet.


5. C_5 is a smooth genus-three curve


Let
  f(r)=(r^4-2r^2+5)(5r^4-2r^2+1).


Exact polynomial calculation gives
  gcd(f,f')=1,
and
  Disc(f)=2^60 * 5^2 != 0.                      (229U.9)


Hence f is squarefree of degree 8. The smooth projective model of
  U^2=f(r)
is therefore a hyperelliptic curve of genus
  g=(8-2)/2=3.                                  (229U.10)


RESULT_229U_FIXED_CURVE_SMOOTH=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229U_FIXED_CURVE_GENUS=3.


6. Faltings gives finite rational r-support


By Faltings' theorem (Mordell conjecture), a smooth projective curve of genus greater than 1 over Q has only finitely many Q-rational points.


Applying this to C_5 gives
  C_5(Q) finite.                                 (229U.11)


Therefore the set of rational r that can occur in a norm-five physical dependence endpoint is finite.


No effective enumeration of C_5(Q) is claimed or needed for the exponent statement.


RESULT_229U_NORM5_RATIONAL_r_SUPPORT=FINITE_BY_FALTINGS.


7. Finite r implies finite realized twist support


For every surviving rational r, 229T also has
  r=epsilon t^2
with at most finitely many rational t.


The rational point Q=(dr,y_Q) on E_d satisfies
  (y_Q/d)^2=d*r*(r^2-1).                        (229U.12)


Thus the squareclass of d in Q^*/Q^{*2} is uniquely determined by r:
  [d]=[r(r^2-1)]                                (229U.13)
because inversion is identical in the squareclass group.


The canonical positive squarefree representative d is therefore unique if it exists. Hence the norm-five physical dependence branch realizes only finitely many canonical twists d.


RESULT_229U_NORM5_REALIZED_TWIST_SUPPORT=FINITE.


This is stronger than the 229T finite-degree/genus-one carrier statement: the surviving physical base selector has converted the moving norm-five branch into a finite twist-support set.


8. Endpoint count on the norm-five dependence branch


Retain 229L: for every fixed canonical twist d, the number of positive physical endpoints of height R_phys<=B mapping to E_d is uniformly
  B^{o(1)}.


Section 7 leaves only finitely many d on the norm-five dependence branch. Therefore


  #{positive physical endpoints R_phys<=B
      in CM dependence with N(alpha)=5}
    = B^{o(1)}
    = o(B^{1/3}).                                (229U.14)


All finitely many norm-five associates/conjugates and physical signs are absorbed into the constant.

  2P=[alpha]R+T,                                (229T.1)
with R in E_d(Q), T in E[2], and N(alpha) odd.


Because deg[alpha]=N(alpha) is odd, [alpha] acts bijectively on E[2]. Hence there is S in E[2] with
  [alpha]S=T.
Replacing R by
  R':=R+S
gives
  2P=[alpha]R'.                                 (229T.2)


Since alpha is coprime to 2 in Z[i], choose u,v in Z[i] with
  2u+alpha v=1.                                 (229T.3)
Define
  Q=[u]R'+[v]P.
Then
  [alpha]Q=P,
  [2]Q=R' in E_d(Q).                            (229T.4)


Conversely, if for some non-torsion Q in E_d(Q(i))
  P=[alpha]Q,
  [2]Q=R in E_d(Q),                             (229T.5)
then sigma(Q)-Q is in E[2]. Writing alpha=a-ib gives
  A=P+sigma(P)=aR+torsion,
  C=iota(P-sigma(P))=bR+torsion,
so A,C are dependent with slope alpha.


Therefore, for every primitive odd-norm slope alpha,


  CM dependence with slope alpha
  <==>
  P lies in [alpha]E_d(Q(i)) with an alpha-preimage Q whose double is rational.


RESULT_229T_ODD_NORM_PULLBACK_EQUIVALENCE=PROVED_EXACT.


This removes the residual T in (229S.11) for all odd slopes and replaces the dependence condition by a fixed CM-divisibility problem plus one rational-double condition.


3. Rational-double cocycle packet


Let
  r:=x(Q)/d in Q(i).
Since 2Q is rational,
  sigma(Q)=Q+S
for some S in E[2].


Using the retained normalized 2-torsion translation formulas, the four possible cocycles give


  S=O:   bar(r)=r;
  S=T0:  bar(r)=-1/r;
  S=T+:  bar(r)=(r+1)/(r-1);
  S=T-:  bar(r)=(1-r)/(1+r).                   (229T.6)


The T0 case is impossible immediately because it gives
  r bar(r)=-1.


The two remaining nontrivial cases are equivalent to


  S=T+:  N(r-1)=2,
  S=T-:  N(r+1)=2.                              (229T.7)


RESULT_229T_RATIONAL_DOUBLE_COCYCLE_PACKET=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Exact norm-five CM x-map


The primitive Gaussian slopes of norm 5 are, up to sign,
  2+i, 2-i, 1+2i, 1-2i.


For alpha=2+i, a direct addition calculation on
  E_d:Y^2=X^3-d^2X
with normalized coordinate r=x(Q)/d gives


  x([2+i]Q)/d
   = r *
     [ ((2-i)r^2+i)(r^2-1+2i)
        /(5r^4-2r^2+1) ]^2.                    (229T.8)


For alpha=2-i the formula is the coefficient conjugate. The slopes 1+2i and 1-2i are obtained by composition with [i], which multiplies normalized x by -1; since -1=i^2 is a square in Q(i), all four norm-five maps have the form


  x([alpha]Q)/d = r H_alpha(r)^2               (229T.9)


for an explicit H_alpha in Q(i)(r).


On the positive physical 229L image,
  x(P)/d=p^2
is a nonzero square in Q(i). Since P is non-torsion, the numerator/denominator exceptional torsion values in (229T.8) are absent. Therefore


  r=x(Q)/d is itself a square in Q(i).           (229T.10)


RESULT_229T_NORM5_XMAP_SQUARE_FACTOR=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229T_NORM5_PREIMAGE_X_IS_GAUSSIAN_SQUARE=PROVED_EXACT.


5. 2-adic lemma: N(s^2 plus/minus 1) cannot equal 2


Let K=Q(i), pi=1+i, and normalize v_pi(pi)=1. Then
  v_2(N_{K/Q}(z))=v_pi(z).


LEMMA 229T.1.
For every s in K,
  v_pi(s^2-1) != 1,
  v_pi(s^2+1) != 1.                             (229T.11)


Proof.
If v_pi(s)>0, then s^2 has positive even valuation and s^2 plus/minus 1 is a unit, so the valuation is 0.


If v_pi(s)<0, then s^2 dominates plus/minus 1 and
  v_pi(s^2 plus/minus 1)=2v_pi(s),
which is even.


If v_pi(s)=0, the residue field is F_2. Hence s is congruent to 1 mod pi; also i is congruent to 1 mod pi. Thus
  s^2-1=(s-1)(s+1)
has both factors divisible by pi, and
  s^2+1=(s-i)(s+i)
also has both factors divisible by pi. In either case the valuation is at least 2.


So valuation 1 never occurs. Consequently
  N(s^2-1) != 2,
  N(s^2+1) != 2.                                (229T.12)


RESULT_229T_2ADIC_NORM2_SQUARE_LEMMA=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Norm-five nontrivial rational-double cocycles are empty


By Section 4 write
  r=s^2
with s in Q(i)^*.


If the rational-double cocycle were T+, then (229T.7) gives
  N(s^2-1)=2,
contradicting Lemma 229T.1.


If the cocycle were T-, then
  N(s^2+1)=2,
again impossible.


T0 was already impossible.


Therefore only
  sigma(Q)=Q
remains, so


  Q in E_d(Q).                                  (229T.13)


RESULT_229T_NORM5_NONTRIVIAL_2DIVISION_COCYCLES=PHYSICALLY_EMPTY_EXACT.
RESULT_229T_NORM5_CM_PREIMAGE_IS_RATIONAL=PROVED_EXACT.


This is a strict strengthening of 229S for N(alpha)=5.


7. Rational normalized square classification


For norm-five dependence we now have Q rational and
  r=x(Q)/d in Q
while r is a square in Q(i).


If s=a+ib in Q(i) and s^2 is rational, then 2ab=0. Hence every rational Gaussian square is either a positive rational square or the negative of one.


Thus there are
  epsilon in {+1,-1},
  t in Q^*
such that
  x(Q)/d=epsilon t^2.                            (229T.14)


Write Q=(d epsilon t^2,y_Q). Since Q is non-torsion, t is nonzero. The curve equation gives


  y_Q^2
   =d^3 epsilon t^2(t^4-1).


Set
  W=y_Q/(dt) in Q.
Then exactly


  W^2=d(t^4-1)        if epsilon=+1,
  W^2=d(1-t^4)        if epsilon=-1.             (229T.15)


Therefore every physical norm-five dependence endpoint lies above one of the two rational genus-one quartic-twist carriers


  C_d^+: W^2=d(t^4-1),
  C_d^-: W^2=d(1-t^4),                           (229T.16)


together with one of the four norm-five CM maps alpha and the retained physical selector conditions on
  P=[alpha]Q.


RESULT_229T_NORM5_DEPENDENCE_REDUCED_TO_RATIONAL_QUARTIC_TWIST_CARRIERS=PROVED_EXACT.


Important: (229T.16) is a NECESSARY carrier reduction for the physical dependence locus, not an assertion that every rational point on these quartics maps to a physical endpoint.


8. Consequence for BOUNDED_CM_IMAGE_GATE


The first surviving Gaussian norm after 229S is no longer an opaque degree-five CM image.


For N(alpha)=5 the dependence problem is now:


  NORM5_RATIONAL_QUARTIC_GATE:
  count or eliminate positive physical endpoints for which there exist
    alpha in {2+i,2-i,1+2i,1-2i} up to sign,
    epsilon in {+1,-1},
    t,W in Q,
  satisfying
    W^2=d epsilon(t^4-1),
    Q=(d epsilon t^2,y_Q) in E_d(Q),
    P=[alpha]Q,
  plus the retained physical selector/descent conditions defining the 229L image.


The nontrivial Q(i)/Q 2-division cocycles have been eliminated entirely at norm 5. The remaining obstruction is purely rational and genus-one.


This does NOT yet supply a same-physical count. In particular:
- a genus-one carrier is not automatically sparse enough;
- fixed degree still earns no counting credit;
- no rank>=2 theorem is authorized merely from this reduction;
- norms >=10/13/... within M_delta remain untreated.


9. Route consequence


The preferred whole-endpoint gate remains


  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(eR_phys,xy))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3)).


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


The next dependence targets are now ordered:


(A) NORM5_RATIONAL_QUARTIC_GATE:
    exploit the explicit rational quartics (229T.16) together with P=[alpha]Q and the physical selector conditions;


(B) odd higher norms:
    reuse the exact odd-norm pullback equivalence (229T.4)-(229T.5);


(C) even remaining norms:

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229S — bounded Gaussian dependence slopes and norm-two exclusion


STATUS: POST_229R_CM_DEPENDENCE_REDUCTION_COMPLETE / PROVED_EXACT_GAUSSIAN_DEPENDENCE_NORMAL_FORM / PROVED_LARGE_TAIL_DEPENDENCE_SLOPES_BOUNDED_INDEPENDENT_OF_B / PROVED_NORM2_GAUSSIAN_SLOPE_PHYSICALLY_EMPTY / REMAINING_BOUNDED_NORM_GE_5_CM_IMAGE_CARRIERS_OPEN / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229R CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE REDUCTION / CANONICAL-HEIGHT BUDGET / SELECTOR-EXACT SMALL-SLOPE EXCLUSION / FIXED-DEGREE CARRIER FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229R
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229R proved that on the positive physical 229L congruent-number twist population with squarefree d>1,
  A=P+sigma(P),
  C=iota(P-sigma(P))
are BOTH non-torsion points of E_d(Q), where
  K=Q(i),
  iota=[i],
  E_d:Y^2=X^3-d^2X.
It also proved
  hhat(A)+hhat(C)=4 hhat(P).                    (229S.1)


The remaining structural subgate was whether A,C can be dependent modulo rational torsion. This card gives an exact dependence normal form, proves that on the current large-d tail only finitely many Gaussian slopes can occur independently of B, and eliminates the smallest possible slope norm exactly from the physical selector equations.


No endpoint saving is claimed.


2. Exact Gaussian dependence normal form


Assume A,C are dependent modulo torsion. Work in the free lattice
  E_d(Q)/E_d(Q)_tors.
Let the saturated rank-one subgroup containing A,C be generated by the class of a non-torsion R in E_d(Q).


Then there are nonzero coprime integers a,b and rational torsion points T_A,T_C such that
  A=aR+T_A,
  C=bR+T_C,
  gcd(a,b)=1,
  ab!=0.                                        (229S.2)


The nonzero assertion uses 229R: neither A nor C is torsion.


For squarefree d>1, retain the 229Q torsion firewall
  E_d(Q(i))_tors=E_d[2].
Using 229Q/229R
  2P=A-iota(C),
we obtain exactly
  2P=[a-ib]R+T,                                 (229S.3)
where
  T=T_A-iota(T_C) in E_d[2].


Thus every dependent physical point lies on a Gaussian multiplication/division carrier with primitive Gaussian slope
  alpha=a-ib in Z[i],
  N(alpha)=a^2+b^2.


RESULT_229S_GAUSSIAN_DEPENDENCE_NORMAL_FORM=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Exact height identity for the dependence coefficients


Torsion has canonical height zero, so from (229S.2)
  hhat(A)=a^2 hhat(R),
  hhat(C)=b^2 hhat(R).
Combining with (229S.1),
  (a^2+b^2) hhat(R)=4 hhat(P).                  (229S.4)


This is exact. In particular the Gaussian norm is not an auxiliary parameter: it is exactly the ratio
  N(alpha)=4 hhat(P)/hhat(R).                   (229S.5)


RESULT_229S_SLOPE_HEIGHT_IDENTITY=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Uniform lower height on the quadratic-twist family


Use the standard fixed-base quadratic-twist canonical-height lower bound recorded in Nara, Remark 1.2, citing Silverman AEC Exercise 8.16(c).


Nara records, in his normalization,
  hhat_N(R) > (1/4) log d + O_E(1)
for non-torsion rational R on a quadratic twist by squarefree d, and explicitly notes that his canonical height is twice the Silverman-standard normalization.


Therefore in the standard Stage37 normalization there is a fixed constant C_E such that
  hhat(R) >= (1/8) log d - C_E                 (229S.6)
for every non-torsion R in E_d(Q).


This use is the general quadratic-twist bound from Nara Remark 1.2; it does NOT invoke Nara Theorem 1.1 or its sixth-power-free discriminant hypothesis.


Retain from 229Q the coarse physical canonical-height adapter: for an absolute Stage37 chart constant C_ph and fixed C_1,
  hhat(P) <= C_ph log B + C_1.                  (229S.7)


RESULT_229S_UNIFORM_RATIONAL_GENERATOR_HEIGHT_LOWER_BOUND=APPLICABLE.


5. Large radical tail implies finitely many dependence slopes


Let
  kappa=1/3-delta >0
and work on the current preferred large-radical tail
  K_*=sf(gcd(eR_phys,xy)) > B^kappa.


Retain 229M/N/O/Q:
  d=sf(2^epsilon K_*),
so
  d >= K_*/2 > (1/2) B^kappa.                  (229S.8)


Combining (229S.4), (229S.6), (229S.7), and (229S.8),
  a^2+b^2
  <= 4(C_ph log B+C_1) /
     ((1/8)(kappa log B-log2)-C_E).             (229S.9)


For every fixed delta<1/3, the right side is bounded by a constant M_delta for all sufficiently large B. Hence


  CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE on the large tail
  is contained in a FINITE set of primitive Gaussian slopes
  alpha=a-ib,
  0<|ab|,
  gcd(a,b)=1,
  N(alpha)<=M_delta,                            (229S.10)


where M_delta depends on delta and the retained fixed height constants, but NOT on B.


Equivalently, for finitely many alpha and T in E[2], one only has to consider
  2P-T in [alpha]E_d(Q).                        (229S.11)


RESULT_229S_LARGE_TAIL_GAUSSIAN_SLOPE_SET=FINITE_UNIFORM_IN_B.
RESULT_229S_DEPENDENCE_GATE_REDUCED_TO_BOUNDED_DEGREE_CM_IMAGE_CARRIERS.


This is structural compression only. A finite union of fixed-degree carriers is NOT automatically sparse on the physical endpoint measure and earns no counting credit.


6. Exact exclusion of the smallest possible slope norm


Because a,b are both nonzero and coprime, the smallest possible Gaussian norm is
  a^2+b^2=2,
which forces
  |a|=|b|=1.
Then (229S.2) gives
  C=+A+T
or
  C=-A+T
for some rational T in E[2].                    (229S.12)


We prove that both possibilities are physically impossible.


Write
  z=p^2=X(P)/d,
  w=conj(z)=X(sigma P)/d.
Retain from 229J/L that p has positive nonzero real and imaginary parts, and
  N(p), N(p^2+1), N(p^2-1)
are rational squares.


Translation by the three nonzero rational 2-torsion points
  T0=(0,0), T+=(d,0), T-=(-d,0)
acts on normalized x-coordinate u=X/d as
  u,
  -1/u,
  (u+1)/(u-1),
  (1-u)/(1+u).                                  (229S.13)


If C=+A+T, then
  [1+i](iP-sigma P)=T.
If C=-A+T, then
  [1+i](P-i sigma P)=T.
In either case the point inside [1+i](...) is torsion because its image is torsion under an isogeny. By the retained 229Q K-torsion firewall it lies in E[2]. Therefore in BOTH signs
  sigma P = +/- iP + Q
for some Q in E[2].


Since x(+/- iP)=-x(P), (229S.13) gives exactly four possibilities:
  w=-z,
  w=1/z,
  w=(z-1)/(z+1),
  w=(1+z)/(1-z).                                (229S.14)


Each is impossible:


(i) w=-z.
Since w=conj(z), z is purely imaginary. With
  p=lambda(x+i y), lambda>0
on the physical chart, Re(p^2)=0 forces x=y.
But the retained missing-face square has
  z_face^2=x^2+y^2=2x^2,
impossible for positive integers x,z_face.


(ii) w=1/z.
Then
  zw=1.
But
  zw=(p conj(p))^2=N(p)^2=v^4,
with
  v=(R_phys+e)/z_face>1
because R_phys^2=e^2+z_face^2 and e>0. Contradiction.


(iii) w=(z-1)/(z+1).
Then
  N(p^2+1)=(z+1)(w+1)=2z.
The left side is rational, so z is rational, contradicting that p^2 is non-real.


(iv) w=(1+z)/(1-z).
Then
  N(p^2-1)=(z-1)(w-1)=-2z.
Again z would be rational, contradiction.


Hence
  N(alpha)=2
is EMPTY on the positive physical population.   (229S.15)


Since norms 1,3,4 cannot occur with coprime nonzero a,b, any dependent physical point satisfies
  N(alpha)=a^2+b^2 >=5.                         (229S.16)


RESULT_229S_NORM2_DEPENDENCE_SLOPE=PHYSICALLY_EMPTY_EXACT.
RESULT_229S_DEPENDENT_PHYSICAL_GAUSSIAN_NORM_LOWER_BOUND=5.


7. What changed and what remains open


Changed:
- 229R's abstract CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE is now a finite bounded-slope problem on the current large radical tail;
- every dependent endpoint has exact normal form
    2P=[alpha]R+T
  with alpha in a B-independent finite set;
- the minimal norm-2 slope is eliminated exactly by the physical selector/missing-face conditions;
- any remaining dependence slope has Gaussian norm at least 5.


Still open:
- slopes of norms 5,10,13,... up to the finite bound M_delta are not eliminated;
- no theorem currently counts the physical points satisfying
    2P-T in [alpha]E_d(Q)
  with the required o(B^(1/3)) total;
- finite-degree carrier reduction alone is not a saving;
- A,C independence is NOT proved globally;
- no rank>=2 route is reopened.


The next high-value dependence attack is no longer an infinite slope problem. It is:


  BOUNDED_CM_IMAGE_GATE:
  for each primitive Gaussian alpha with
    5<=N(alpha)<=M_delta
  and each T in E[2],
  count or eliminate physical endpoints on the exact same measure satisfying
    2P-T in [alpha]E_d(Q).


A uniform elimination, or an o(B^(1/3)) total over this finite set, would close CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE and permit a legitimate reassessment of independent-pair/rank>=2 inputs.


Do not infer sparsity merely from finite degree, and do not issue M3-T11-230 from this reduction alone.


8. Route consequence


The preferred gate remains exactly
  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R_phys<=B:
      sf(gcd(eR_phys,xy))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    =o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD remains CONDITIONAL_RESERVE/THEOREM_WATCH.


Useful future inputs:
(A) direct elimination/count of the finite BOUNDED_CM_IMAGE_GATE;
(B) a selector-conditioned rational small-point/twist-support theorem;
(C) sharper physical height-vs-d lowering M_delta enough to exhaust all slopes;
(D) direct same-physical radical-support theorem.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


9. Sources checked

External theorem input:

Nara, “Lower bounds of the canonical height on quadratic twists of elliptic curves,” arXiv:1110.6710, Remark 1.2, which records the general fixed-base quadratic-twist lower bound from Silverman, Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, Exercise 8.16(c), and states Nara's normalization is twice the standard Silverman normalization.


AUDIT SCOPE


This card is an exact dependence normal-form theorem, a uniform large-tail bounded-slope deduction, and an exact norm-2 physical exclusion. It does not prove an endpoint saving, does not establish full CM-pair independence, does not change the preferred radical-gcd gate, does not retract 229L-R, and does not issue M3-T11-230. Integrated audit186–229O remains unchanged in scope.

229Q proved that for the 229L congruent-number twist
  E_d: Y^2=X^3-d^2 X
over K=Q(i), the CM trace/anti-trace construction sends a non-torsion P in E_d(K) to at least one non-torsion point of E_d(Q). It also proved that for positive squarefree d>1 the physical 229L point P is non-torsion.


This card uses the full selector conditions retained from 229J/L,
  N(p) in Q^{*2},
  N(p^2+1) in Q^{*2},
  N(p^2-1) in Q^{*2},
together with positivity/non-boundary, to prove more: BOTH rational CM components are non-torsion. It then records the exact canonical-height sum and a support-count firewall.


No endpoint saving is claimed.


2. Setup and exact CM pair


Let sigma be complex conjugation and
  iota(X,Y)=(-X,iY)
the j=1728 CM automorphism of E_d over K.


For the physical P in E_d(K), write
  X(P)/d = p^2 =: z,
  X(sigma P)/d = q^2 =: w,
where q=conj(p), and p has nonzero positive real and imaginary parts on the positive physical chamber.


Define
  A=P+sigma(P),
  C=iota(P-sigma(P)).
As in 229Q,
  A,C in E_d(Q),
and
  2P=A-iota(C).                                  (229R.1)


Retain the 229Q torsion firewall
  E_d(Q)_tors=E_d[2]
for positive squarefree d>1.


3. Translation by rational 2-torsion gives four Möbius transforms


Let
  T0=(0,0), T+=(d,0), T-=(-d,0).


For any non-2-torsion point with normalized x-coordinate z=X/d, translation by these points has normalized x-coordinate


  x(P+T0)/d = -1/z,
  x(P+T+)/d = (z+1)/(z-1),
  x(P+T-)/d = (1-z)/(1+z).                     (229R.2)


The point at infinity gives the identity transform z.


Because x(-P+T)=x(P+T), the same four transforms occur if
  sigma(P)=T-P
or
  sigma(P)=P+T.


RESULT_229R_2TORSION_MOBIUS_PACKET=PROVED_EXACT.


4. The trace A cannot be torsion


Assume A is torsion. By the retained rational torsion statement, A is one of
  O,T0,T+,T-.
Since A=P+sigma(P), this gives sigma(P)=A-P. Hence w must be one of the four transforms in Section 3.


Case A=O:
  w=z.
Then z is real. But z=p^2 and p has nonzero real and imaginary parts, so p^2 is non-real. Contradiction.


Case A=T0:
  w=-1/z.
Then
  zw=-1.
But zw=p^2 q^2=N(p)^2 is a positive rational square. Contradiction.


Case A=T+:
  w=(z+1)/(z-1).
Then
  N(p^2-1)
   =(z-1)(w-1)
   =2.
But the physical selector requires N(p^2-1) in Q^{*2}, and 2 is not a rational square. Contradiction.


Case A=T-:
  w=(1-z)/(1+z).
Then
  N(p^2+1)
   =(z+1)(w+1)
   =2,
again contradicting the selector square condition.


Therefore
  A is non-torsion.                                (229R.3)


RESULT_229R_TRACE_NONTORSION=PROVED_EXACT_ON_PHYSICAL_d_GT_1.


5. The anti-trace C cannot be torsion


Assume C is torsion. Since iota permutes E_d[2],
  P-sigma(P)=iota^{-1}(C)
is a rational 2-torsion point T.
Hence
  sigma(P)=P-T=P+T.
Taking x-coordinates gives exactly the same four Möbius transforms of Section 3.


The four contradictions from Section 4 therefore apply verbatim:
- identity transform makes p^2 real;
- T0 gives N(p)^2=-1;
- T+ forces N(p^2-1)=2;
- T- forces N(p^2+1)=2.


Therefore
  C is non-torsion.                                (229R.4)


RESULT_229R_ANTITRACE_NONTORSION=PROVED_EXACT_ON_PHYSICAL_d_GT_1.
RESULT_229R_BOTH_Q_RATIONAL_COMPONENTS_NONTORSION=PROVED_EXACT.


This is strictly stronger than the 229Q statement “at least one is non-torsion.” It is a refinement, not a retraction.


6. Exact canonical-height sum and improved one-point height transfer


The CM automorphism iota has degree 1 and preserves canonical height. Also sigma preserves canonical height. Therefore


  hhat(C)=hhat(P-sigma(P)).


By the parallelogram identity,


  hhat(A)+hhat(C)
   =hhat(P+sigma(P))+hhat(P-sigma(P))
   =2hhat(P)+2hhat(sigma(P))
   =4hhat(P).                                     (229R.5)


Since both A and C are non-torsion, both heights are strictly positive. In particular,


  min(hhat(A),hhat(C)) <= 2 hhat(P).              (229R.6)


Thus the rational small-point transfer in 229Q improves from the safe factor 4 to factor 2 for the physical d>1 population.


RESULT_229R_CM_HEIGHT_SUM=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229R_RATIONAL_SMALL_POINT_FACTOR=2_INSTEAD_OF_4.


This changes no Stage37 exponent by itself because 229L only supplies hhat(P)=O(log B), and 229Q already showed that the retained d<=2B^2 envelope is far outside the Le Boudec one-third budget even in the optimistic alpha->0 limit.


7. Important non-claim: no rank-two conclusion


A and C are both non-torsion, but this does NOT prove that they are independent in E_d(Q) modulo torsion.


They may lie in the same rank-one Mordell-Weil line. Therefore this card does not route physical twists into the rank>=2 twist subfamily and does not invoke any rank-two density theorem.


Define the remaining CM-pair structural question:


  CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE:
  control the physical endpoints for which A and C are dependent modulo E_d(Q)_tors.


A proof that dependence is impossible or sufficiently sparse would be genuinely new input. No such statement is proved here.


RESULT_229R_CM_PAIR_INDEPENDENCE=OPEN.


8. Positive-rank support alone cannot be the missing theorem


Alexander Smith proved that congruent numbers have positive natural density; in particular, a positive proportion of squarefree d give E_d(Q) a non-torsion rational point.


Therefore an unconditioned theorem that merely counts squarefree twists d<=X with E_d(Q) non-torsion cannot have o(X) support. At the Stage37 ambient envelope X~B^2 this is vastly too large.


Consequently the CM rationalization must retain genuinely restrictive information:
- the inherited small-height relation,
- the physical selector/descent origin,
- the radical-gcd realization,
- or an equally strong same-physical condition.


Discarding these and counting all positive-rank congruent twists is a mathematically invalid route to the Stage37 B^(1/3) target.


RESULT_229R_POSITIVE_RANK_SUPPORT_FIREWALL=PROVED_BY_EXISTING_POSITIVE_DENSITY_THEOREM.


9. Route consequence


The preferred whole-endpoint theorem gate remains unchanged:


  #{positive primitive physical endpoints R<=B :
      sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}
    = o(B^(1/3))


for some fixed delta>0.


229R sharpens the rationalized twist side as follows:


- Q(i)-to-Q field mismatch remains retired.
- Both canonical rational CM components are non-torsion.
- The best guaranteed rational small point has canonical height at most 2 hhat(P), improving the 229Q factor 4.
- Existence of a rational point alone is provably too broad because congruent twists have positive density.
- The new exact structural subgate is CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE, but no automatic production continuation is authorized.


Useful future inputs include:
(A) a physical selector-conditioned small-point theorem over Q retaining the 229L/229M descent labels;
(B) a proof that the dependent CM-pair locus is empty or o(B^(1/3)), followed by a quantitatively strong independent-pair/rank>=2 theorem;
(C) a sharper physical height-vs-d relation that places the rational CM component in a Le Boudec-compatible regime;
(D) a direct same-physical twist/radical-support theorem.


Do not reopen:
- generic positive-rank congruent-number support counting;
- unconditioned all-twist small-point counting at d<=2B^2;
- rank>=2 counting without first proving A,C independence on the relevant physical population.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


10. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229Q;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229L;
- retained 229M/N/O twist/radical identification;
- current MAIN / CARD-INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE.


External:
- Pierre Le Boudec, “Height of rational points on quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve,” Bull. London Math. Soc. 48 (2016), 99–108, arXiv:1404.7738. Retained 229Q theorem budget.
- Alexander Smith, “The congruent numbers have positive natural density,” arXiv:1603.08479, revised 2026. Used only for the positive-rank support firewall.


AUDIT SCOPE


This card proves an exact strengthening of the 229Q CM decomposition on the physical selector population. It does not improve the endpoint exponent, does not establish CM-pair independence, does not change the preferred radical-gcd gate, does not retract 229L-Q, and does not issue M3-T11-230. Integrated audit186–229O remains unchanged in scope.




FINAL_READBACK_RECEIPT: PASS.
Card identity/title/content read back from Drive. CARD-INDEX row483 and 案内 latest/read-order point to 229R. MAIN contains CURRENT AUTHORITY OVERRIDE=229R with unchanged preferred sf(gcd(eR,xy)) gate, T11-230 unissued, PRIMARY_GATE OPEN and GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0. RESULT-LEDGER contains the 229R change record and card pointer. Active ROUTE contains the POST-229R selector-exact CM-pair block, CM_PAIR_DEPENDENCE_GATE firewall and unchanged GAUSSIAN_TWIST_RADICAL_GCD conditional-reserve status. Both rational CM components non-torsion, exact height sum hhat(A)+hhat(C)=4hhat(P), factor-2 small-point transfer, positive-rank-support firewall, and no-rank>=2 nonclaim are all present. Integrated audit186–229O remains limited to its stated scope and is not silently extended to 229P–R. Production HOLD retained; P/M3 limit unproved.

records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229Q — CM rationalization and small-point twist budget ceiling
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229Q — CM rationalization and small-point twist budget ceiling


STATUS: POST_229P_CM_TWIST_AUDIT_COMPLETE / PROVED_QI_TO_Q_TRACE_ANTITRACE_RATIONALIZATION / PROVED_PHYSICAL_TAIL_TWIST_POINT_NONTORSION_FOR_d_GT_1 / LE_BOUDEC_RATIONAL_SMALL_POINT_THEOREM_NOW_CONTRACT_MATCHES_FIELD_BUT_EXPONENT_NO_GO_AT_CURRENT_d_SCALE / CHAN_INTEGRAL_POINT_THEOREMS_NOT_DIRECTLY_APPLICABLE / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229P MOVING-TWIST SUPPORT AUDIT / CM DESCENT / TORSION FIREWALL / CURRENT SMALL-POINT THEOREM BUDGET CHECK
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229P
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229L gives, for every positive physical endpoint, a canonical positive squarefree twist d and a point
  P in E_d(Q(i)),   E_d: Y^2=X^3-d^2 X,
with inherited exponential height B^O(1), O(1) endpoint-to-point multiplicity, and uniform fixed-d endpoint fiber B^o(1). 229M/N/O identify d up to the harmless 2-adic squareclass with
  K_*=sf(gcd(eR,xy)),
and give d <= 2B^2. 229P shows that ordinary base codimension-two sieving cannot close the large-K_* tail.


The first question here is whether the field Q(i) blocks the strong literature on rational points in congruent-number twist families. It does not: the j=1728 CM automorphism gives an exact rationalization to Q. The second question is whether current small-point theorems then meet the Stage37 B^(1/3) budget. They do not at the current twist scale.


No endpoint saving is claimed.


2. Exact CM trace/anti-trace rationalization


Let K=Q(i), let sigma be complex conjugation, and let
  iota:E_d -> E_d,
  iota(X,Y)=(-X,iY).
Then sigma(iota)=-iota and iota^2=[-1].


For P in E_d(K), define
  A=P+sigma(P),
  C=iota(P-sigma(P)).
Then A is sigma-invariant, hence A in E_d(Q). Also
  sigma(C)=(-iota)(sigma(P)-P)=iota(P-sigma(P))=C,
so C in E_d(Q).


Moreover
  2P = A - iota(C).
Indeed -iota(C)=P-sigma(P).


Therefore if P is non-torsion, at least one of A,C is a non-torsion Q-rational point. Otherwise A and C would both be torsion and the displayed identity would force 2P, hence P, to be torsion.


Canonical height is preserved by sigma and by the degree-one automorphism iota. The parallelogram inequality gives
  hhat(A) <= 2(hhat(P)+hhat(sigma P)) = 4 hhat(P),
  hhat(C) = hhat(P-sigma P) <= 4 hhat(P).
Thus a non-torsion physical P of exponential height <=B^C produces a non-torsion Q-rational point on the same E_d of exponential canonical height <=B^(4C).


RESULT_229Q_CM_RATIONALIZATION=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229Q_Q_RATIONAL_HEIGHT_TRANSFER=PROVED_WITH_FACTOR_4_IN_CANONICAL_HEIGHT.


This is stronger than merely using the quadratic-extension rank formula: it gives explicit rational points and a height comparison on the same twist.


3. Physical tail points are non-torsion over Q(i)


For positive squarefree d, the rational torsion of the congruent-number curve is
  E_d(Q)_tors={O,(0,0),(d,0),(-d,0)}.


We prove that for d>1,
  E_d(Q(i))_tors=E_d[2].


First, there is no odd-order torsion over Q(i). If T has odd order, then
  T+sigma(T) in E_d(Q),
  iota(T-sigma(T)) in E_d(Q)
are odd-order rational torsion, hence both O. The identity
  2T=(T+sigma T)-iota(iota(T-sigma T))
then forces 2T=O, so T=O.


Second, there is no point of order 4 for squarefree d>1. A 2-torsion point (r,0) on
  Y^2=(X-0)(X-d)(X+d)
is divisible by 2 over a field of characteristic not 2 only if the two root differences from r are squares in that field. Thus:
- halving (0,0) requires d and -d square in Q(i);
- halving (d,0) requires d and 2d square in Q(i);
- halving (-d,0) requires -d and -2d square in Q(i).
For a positive rational d, d is a square in Q(i) iff it is a rational square. Hence for positive squarefree d>1 none of these conditions can hold. Any torsion of 2-power order >2 would contain a point of order 4, so no such torsion exists.


The 229L physical image is never 2-torsion: X/d=p^2, while p=0 is outside the physical torus and p^2=1 or -1 forces a zero physical edge, already proved impossible in 229L. Therefore every physical 229L point with d>1 is non-torsion.


On the current preferred large-radical tail, d is comparable to K_* up to a factor of 2 through d=sf(2^epsilon K_*), so for B large the tail automatically has d>1.


RESULT_229Q_PHYSICAL_TAIL_POINT_NONTORSION=PROVED.
RESULT_229Q_QI_TORSION_FIREWALL=FOR_SQUAREFREE_d_GT_1_ONLY_FULL_2_TORSION.


4. Le Boudec 2016 now matches the field, but not the Stage37 exponent


Le Boudec studies the Q-rational congruent-number twist family in the equivalent model
  d y^2=x^3-x
and defines N_alpha^*(X) by summing non-torsion rational points of exponential canonical height at most d^(1/8+alpha) over squarefree d<=X. For the full rational 2-torsion family he proves, for fixed alpha>0 and epsilon>0,
  N_alpha^*(X) << X^(1/2+alpha+epsilon).


Sections 2-3 remove the previous Q(i)-versus-Q quantifier mismatch: every physical tail twist d now genuinely contributes a non-torsion Q-rational point on E_d, with polynomial physical-B height.


However the exponent budget is still wrong. Current Stage37 only has
  d <= 2B^2.
Even in the formally best possible limit alpha -> 0+, the Le Boudec bound at X~B^2 is only
  B^(1+o(1)),
far above the required o(B^(1/3)) twist-support budget.


The actual physical height transfer is weaker still: if hhat(P)<=C log B and the large-radical tail begins at d >= c B^kappa with kappa=1/3-delta, then a uniform use of Le Boudec over the whole tail requires a fixed
  alpha >= 4C/kappa - 1/8
(up to harmless constants), which only increases the exponent.


A useful budget corollary is exact at the method level. If an independent argument truncated every realized physical twist to
  d <= B^beta
and one could work in the near-minimal alpha->0 regime, Le Boudec's X^(1/2+alpha) mechanism could beat B^(1/3) only if
  beta < 2/3.
More generally the condition is
  beta(1/2+alpha) < 1/3.
The current beta=2 envelope is far outside this range.


RESULT_229Q_LE_BOUDEC_FIELD_CONTRACT=NOW_MATCHES_AFTER_CM_DESCENT.
RESULT_229Q_LE_BOUDEC_DIRECT_STAGE37_MATCH=NO_GO_AT_CURRENT_TWIST_SCALE.
RESULT_229Q_LE_BOUDEC_BETA_THRESHOLD=beta(1/2+alpha)<1/3; OPTIMISTIC_ALPHA_TO_0_REQUIRES_beta<2/3.


This is a theorem-budget no-go, not an impossibility theorem for a new small-point estimate on the much thinner physical 2-descent image.


5. Integral-point results do not black-box transfer


Chan's current congruent-number result bounds the total number of non-trivial integral points on E_D for squarefree D<=N by
  O_epsilon(N (log N)^(-0.137061...+epsilon))
(and in the abstract by the weaker displayed O(N(log N)^(-1/4+epsilon)) formulation across versions).


This is a strong average theorem on integral points, but the CM rationalization in Section 2 uses elliptic-curve addition. The resulting rational points A or C are not proved integral, or even uniformly S-integral with bounded S, on the Stage37 physical image. Therefore Chan's theorem does not currently count the realized Stage37 twists.


Even if integrality were granted for free, substituting the present N~B^2 twist envelope yields only B^2 times a logarithmic saving, still far above B^(1/3). The 2025 Browning-Chan “almost all twists have no integral points” theorem has the same integrality mismatch for this route and does not supply the required Stage37 fixed-power exceptional-set rate.


RESULT_229Q_CHAN_INTEGRAL_ADAPTER=NOT_ESTABLISHED.
RESULT_229Q_INTEGRAL_AVERAGE_DIRECT_BUDGET=NO_GO_AT_N_SIM_B2.


6. Consequence for the theorem watch


The CM field mismatch is retired for non-torsion physical tail points. The moving-twist route can now be phrased entirely over Q:


Every endpoint in the current large-K_* tail yields a squarefree d comparable to K_* and a non-torsion rational point on E_d(Q), with a distinguished inherited 2-descent origin and polynomial physical-B height.


What remains missing is not “Q(i) rational points” but a quantitatively much thinner twist-support theorem. A sufficient new input may take one of these forms:


(A) PHYSICAL/DESCENT-CONDITIONED SMALL-POINT TWIST COUNT:
count the squarefree d actually arising from the 229L/229M distinguished physical 2-descent image by o(B^(1/3)), rather than all twists with a small rational point.


(B) LARGE-d DISPOSAL PLUS SMALL-POINT THEOREM:
first prove that all but o(B^(1/3)) physical endpoints have d<=B^(beta) with beta<2/3 (or beta satisfying beta(1/2+alpha)<1/3 at the available height exponent), then Le Boudec-type bounds become budget-compatible in principle.


(C) STRONGER RATIONAL-POINT EXCEPTIONAL-SET THEOREM:
a theorem over Q whose exceptional twist count at the inherited polynomial physical height is itself o(B^(1/3)) over d<=2B^2.


Integral-point sparsity alone is not a restart trigger without an exact integrality/quasi-integrality adapter and a fixed-power rate meeting the Stage37 budget.


The preferred gate remains
  #{primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B:
      sf(gcd(eR,xy))>B^(1/3-delta)}
    = o(B^(1/3))
for some fixed delta>0.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


7. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229P;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229L;
- retained 229M/N/O twist-to-radical identification and d<=2B^2 envelope;
- current MAIN / CARD-INDEX / RESULT-LEDGER / active ROUTE.


External theorem rematch:
- Pierre Le Boudec, “Height of rational points on quadratic twists of a given elliptic curve,” Bull. London Math. Soc. 48 (2016), arXiv:1404.7738. In the congruent-number/full-2-torsion case, N_alpha^*(X)<<X^(1/2+alpha+epsilon).
- Pierre Le Boudec, “Height of rational points on congruent number elliptic curves,” arXiv:1802.07136. Positive-proportion large-minimal-height result; no Stage37-rate exceptional-set transfer obtained here.
- Stephanie Chan, “The average number of integral points on the congruent number curves,” Adv. Math. 457 (2024), arXiv:2112.01615, current arXiv text dated 2026-03-22.
- Tim Browning and Stephanie Chan, “Almost all quadratic twists of an elliptic curve have no integral points,” JEMS, published online 2025, arXiv:2401.04375.


AUDIT SCOPE


This card proves a new exact CM descent and torsion firewall, then performs a quantitative theorem-contract audit. It does not prove a new endpoint saving, does not change the preferred radical-gcd gate, does not retract 229L-P, and does not issue M3-T11-230. Integrated audit 186-229O is not silently extended to 229P-Q.
