﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229P — codimension-two geometric-sieve ceiling and selector-lift necessity


STATUS: POST_229O_GEOMETRIC_SIEVE_PREFLIGHT_COMPLETE / PROVED_EXACT_RANK6_QUADRIC_EMBEDDING / PROVED_BHB_2020_LARGE_PRIME_SUBTAIL_APPLICABILITY / PROVED_AMBIENT_EXPONENT_NO_GO / PROVED_BASE_ONLY_CODIM2_DIVISOR_UNION_CEILING / SELECTOR_OR_SUPPORT_LIFT_REQUIRED / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0
TYPE: POST-229O GEOMETRIC-SIEVE THEOREM CONTRACT / EXACT PHYSICAL AMBIENT ADAPTER / METHOD-BUDGET NO-GO
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229O
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229O reduced the current preferred whole-endpoint gate to


  K_*(E)=sf(gcd(eR,xy)),


and asks, for some fixed δ>0,


  #{primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B :
      K_*(E)>B^(1/3-δ)}
    = o(B^(1/3)).                                  (229P.1)


This card tests a tempting theorem species that was not yet quantitatively closed by 229O: geometric/Ekedahl sieve on a quadric or on the fixed 4A1 toric base.


The outcome is twofold.


First, there is an exact rank-6 quadric enlargement on which the Browning–Heath-Brown geometric sieve is genuinely applicable to the large-prime common-divisor subtail. The resulting ambient exponent is nevertheless far too large for Stage37.


Second, even granting an ideal squarefree-modulus codimension-two estimate on the 229F/229K base, the ordinary divisor-union mechanism misses the B^(1/3) target. Thus merely obtaining a nonsplit analogue of a standard codimension-two geometric sieve on the BASE would not by itself close (229P.1). A future sieve must use the selector lift / twist-support compression / another genuinely stronger same-physical mechanism.


No endpoint exponent is improved here.


2. Exact rank-6 quadric containing every physical endpoint


Use the positive physical endpoint variables


  e,x,y,U,V,R


with


  e^2+x^2=U^2,
  e^2+y^2=V^2,
  e^2+x^2+y^2=R^2.                                (229P.2)


Define


  Q1=e^2+x^2-U^2,
  Q2=e^2+y^2-V^2,
  Q3=e^2+x^2+y^2-R^2,


and take their fixed sum


  Q=Q1+Q2+Q3
   =3e^2+2x^2+2y^2-U^2-V^2-R^2.                  (229P.3)


The diagonal quadratic form Q has six nonzero diagonal coefficients, hence


  rank(Q)=6.                                       (229P.4)


Every physical endpoint satisfies Q=0.


There is no height loss. From (229P.2),


  U^2=R^2-y^2,
  V^2=R^2-x^2,


so on the positive chamber


  0<e,x,y,U,V<=R.


Therefore the exact physical cutoff R<=B implies


  ||(e,x,y,U,V,R)||_∞ <= B.                       (229P.5)


Also any common divisor of all six coordinates divides e,x,y, so the retained primitive condition gcd(e,x,y)=1 makes the six-coordinate vector primitive. Browning–Heath-Brown counts all integral vectors anyway, so primitiveness is not needed for the upper-bound inclusion.


RESULT_229P_RANK6_PHYSICAL_QUADRIC_EMBEDDING=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229P_PHYSICAL_HEIGHT_TO_AMBIENT_SUP_HEIGHT=NO_POWER_LOSS.


3. Exact codimension check for F1=eR and F2=xy


Set


  F1=eR,
  F2=xy.                                           (229P.6)


Then the current 229O common divisor is exactly


  gcd(F1,F2)=gcd(eR,xy).


Consider


  Z={Q=F1=F2=0} subset P^5.


The equations eR=0 and xy=0 split into four codimension-two coordinate linear spaces:


  L_ex : e=x=0,
  L_ey : e=y=0,
  L_Rx : R=x=0,
  L_Ry : R=y=0.


On these four spaces the restriction of Q is respectively


  2y^2-U^2-V^2-R^2,
  2x^2-U^2-V^2-R^2,
  3e^2+2y^2-U^2-V^2,
  3e^2+2x^2-U^2-V^2.                              (229P.7)


None is the zero polynomial. Hence Q cuts each P^3 component by one genuine equation, so every component of Z has dimension at most 2. Therefore


  codim_{P^5}(Z) >= 3.                             (229P.8)


Together with rank(Q)=6, this verifies the hypotheses of Browning–Heath-Brown, Theorem 1.2, for Q,F1,F2.


RESULT_229P_BHB_HYPOTHESES=PROVED_EXACT_FOR_RANK6_ENLARGEMENT.


4. Browning–Heath-Brown controls a large-prime subtail, but at the wrong scale


For a quadratic form in n+1 variables with n=5, Browning–Heath-Brown gives, for the number N(B,M) of integral points on Q=0 for which F1,F2 have a common prime divisor p>M,


  N(B,M)
   << B^(4+ε)/(M log M) + B^(4-1/5+ε)
    = B^(4+ε)/(M log M) + B^(19/5+ε).             (229P.9)


All positive physical endpoints in the corresponding large-prime event are a subset of these ambient points by Sections 2–3.


At the Stage37 radical threshold


  M=B^(1/3-δ),


(229P.9) is only


  << B^(11/3+δ+ε)/(log B) + B^(19/5+ε),           (229P.10)


which is enormously above the required o(B^(1/3)) scale.


Moreover the theorem only catches the event that gcd(eR,xy) has one prime divisor p>M. The current tail K_*>M can also occur when K_* is a product of many primes all <=M. Therefore the direct theorem does not even cover the entire radical tail before the exponent issue is considered.


RESULT_229P_BHB_LARGE_PRIME_SUBTAIL_MATCH=APPLICABLE_BUT_TOO_WEAK.
RESULT_229P_BHB_DIRECT_STAGE37_MATCH=NO_GO.
NO_GO_REASON_1=ambient rank6 quadric population has B^4 scale.
NO_GO_REASON_2=the theorem detects one large common prime, not a large smooth squarefree kernel.


This is a theorem-contract no-go, not an impossibility theorem for a new sieve acting directly on the physical endpoint locus.


5. Base-only codimension-two divisor-union ceiling


The previous failure might suggest transferring a Huang-style or other effective codimension-two geometric sieve directly to the fixed nonsplit 4A1 toric base X0 of 229F/229J/229K, where the exact physical height is R and the retained anticanonical dense-torus base count is B^(1+o(1)) up to polylogarithmic factors.


Grant a theorem stronger than what is currently available: for every relevant squarefree modulus m, uniformly through the required range,


  N_m(B)
   := #{base points H<=B : m|eR and m|xy}
   << B^(1+o(1))/m^σ.                             (229P.11)


For a pure codimension-two local-density model one expects σ=2.


Let


  Y=B^(1/3-δ).


If K_*=sf(gcd(eR,xy))>Y, then the squarefree integer m=K_* itself satisfies m>Y and m|eR, m|xy. Hence the direct divisor-union estimate gives


  # {base points : K_*>Y}
    <= sum_{m>Y} N_m(B)
    << B^(1+o(1)) sum_{m>Y} m^(-σ)
    << B^(1+o(1)) Y^(-(σ-1))                      (229P.12)


for σ>1.


To beat B^(1/3), (229P.12) requires


  1-(σ-1)(1/3-δ) < 1/3,


equivalently


  σ > 1 + 2/(1-3δ).                               (229P.13)


In particular:


- σ=2 gives only B^(2/3+δ+o(1));
- σ=3 gives only B^(1/3+2δ+o(1));
- for every fixed δ>0, the required decay is strictly stronger than cubic in m.


Thus even an ideal composite-modulus version of ordinary codimension-two base equidistribution, with m^(-2) density and perfect uniformity, cannot close the current one-third radical gate through a direct divisor-union argument.


RESULT_229P_BASE_CODIM2_DIVISOR_UNION_CEILING=PROVED_CONDITIONAL_METHOD_BUDGET.
RESULT_229P_REQUIRED_MODULUS_DECAY_SIGMA_GT_1_PLUS_2_OVER_1_MINUS_3DELTA=PROVED.
RESULT_229P_PURE_BASE_SIGMA2_INSUFFICIENT=true.


The word “ceiling” here is method-specific. It does not rule out cancellation, a Selberg/large-sieve mechanism that uses more than the union bound, a support-count theorem, or a theorem operating on the selector cover rather than on the base.


6. Consequence for the Stage37 theorem watch


229P sharpens the current restart contract.


A new nonsplit toric geometric sieve with only the ordinary codimension-two strength of the base is not enough by itself. Likewise the available rank>=5 quadric sieve is not enough after the exact rank-6 ambient embedding.


A useful new input must exploit information beyond the base common-divisor incidence. Sufficient forms include:


(A) SELECTOR-CONDITIONED MODULUS DECAY:
a same-physical theorem for the lifted endpoint/selector population with effective squarefree-modulus decay strong enough to beat (229P.13), or an equivalent estimate after summing moduli;


(B) DIRECT TWIST/RADICAL SUPPORT:
a theorem counting the actually realized K_*=sf(gcd(eR,xy)) or canonical twist classes directly with o(B^(1/3)) support, using 229L's uniform fixed-twist B^o(1) fiber;


(C) STRONGER SUFFICIENT BRANCH:
a theorem on one retained stronger branch, such as the 229M raw content tails, which independently meets the same B^(1/3) budget on the exact physical endpoint measure.


Do not next spend a production card on:
- another generic rank>=5 quadric geometric-sieve embedding;
- a nonsplit base sieve whose only gain is ordinary codimension-two m^(-2) local density;
- a large-prime-only gcd theorem without a smooth-radical treatment;
- multiplying base/local selector densities as independent probabilities.


The preferred gate remains exactly


  PHYSICAL_JOINT_RADICAL_GCD_ONE_THIRD_QUOTIENT_FREE:


  #{primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B :
      sf(gcd(eR,xy))>B^(1/3-δ)}
    = o(B^(1/3))                                  (229P.14)


for some fixed δ>0.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_SELECTOR_AWARE_OR_SUPPORT_LEVEL_THEOREM_INPUT.


7. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229O;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229N;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229M;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229K;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229F;
- M3-T11-228;
- current MAIN / RESULT-LEDGER / CARD-INDEX / active ROUTE.


External theorem rematch:
- Tim Browning and Roger Heath-Brown, “The geometric sieve for quadrics,” arXiv:2003.09593, especially Theorem 1.2.
- Tim Santens, “Manin's conjecture for integral points on toric varieties,” Proc. London Math. Soc. 133 (2026), e70203, used only as retained 229K context for the nonsplit toric base and bounded-height scale.


AUDIT SCOPE


This card gives an exact rank-6 ambient adapter and two scoped method-budget no-go results. It does not prove a new endpoint saving, does not retract 229O or earlier cards, and does not give a perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion. Its substantive effect is to rule out two tempting generic sieve continuations at the current exponent budget and to require future sieve input to be selector-aware, support-level, or otherwise stronger than base codimension-two density.

Card body contains the rank-6 physical quadric adapter, codim>=3 check for Q=eR=xy=0, Browning–Heath-Brown n=5 large-prime bound/no-go, the base-only divisor-union sigma threshold sigma>1+2/(1-3delta), and the selector/support-level restart contract. ﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229O — quotient-free homogeneous GCD adapter and 2026 GCD-theorem no-go


STATUS: POST_229N_QUOTIENT_REMOVAL_COMPLETE / PROVED_GSTAR_EQUALS_GCD_eR_xy / PROVED_HOMOGENEOUS_QUADRATIC_GCD_ADAPTER / YASUFUKU_2026_DIRECT_APPLICATION_INELIGIBLE_AND_EXPONENT_TOO_WEAK / BARRIOS_2026_CORRECTED_COMPONENTWISE_BOUND_TOO_WEAK / LARGE_RADICAL_GCD_TAIL_OPEN / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229N EXACT PHYSICAL GCD SIMPLIFICATION / CURRENT GCD-THEOREM CONTRACT AUDIT / ANTI-LOOP FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229N
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229N reduced the full positive physical endpoint problem to the squarefree kernel
  K_* = sf(G_*),
  G_* = gcd(eR, x'y'),
where
  d0 = gcd(x,y),
  x' = x/d0,
  y' = y/d0,
and showed that
  K_* <= B^(1/3-delta)
is o(M3) by the retained 229L fixed-twist B^o(1) fiber theorem.


The remaining preferred quantitative gate was written as
  sf(gcd(eR, xy/gcd(x,y)^2)) > B^(1/3-delta).


This card proves that the quotient is unnecessary and then rematches the resulting homogeneous GCD against the strongest directly relevant unconditional 2026 GCD-height theorems found in the current scan.


2. The missing-face common content is coprime to both e and R


Let
  d0 = gcd(x,y).
The retained primitive physical condition is
  gcd(e,x,y)=1.


Since d0 divides x and y,
  gcd(e,d0)=1.                                      (229O.1)


Now suppose a prime p divides both R and d0. Then p divides R,x,y. The physical sphere equation
  R^2 = e^2 + x^2 + y^2
implies
  e^2 == 0 mod p,
hence p divides e. This contradicts gcd(e,x,y)=1.


Therefore
  gcd(R,d0)=1.                                      (229O.2)


Combining (229O.1) and (229O.2),
  gcd(eR,d0)=1.                                     (229O.3)


RESULT_229O_D0_COPRIME_TO_eR=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Exact quotient removal


Because
  x = d0 x',
  y = d0 y',
we have
  xy = d0^2 x'y'.


By (229O.3), d0^2 is coprime to eR. Therefore
  gcd(eR,xy)
    = gcd(eR,d0^2 x'y')
    = gcd(eR,x'y')
    = G_*.                                          (229O.4)


Hence the 229N twist-support invariant has the quotient-free form
  G_* = gcd(eR,xy),                                 (229O.5)
  K_* = sf(gcd(eR,xy)),                             (229O.6)
and
  d = sf(2^epsilon gcd(eR,xy)).                     (229O.7)


The preferred full-endpoint tail can therefore be rewritten exactly as
  P_rad-tail(B)
   = # {primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B:
        sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}.            (229O.8)


No denominator, normalized leg, or rational polynomial is required in the theorem-facing GCD expression.


RESULT_229O_GSTAR_EQUALS_GCD_eR_xy=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229O_QUOTIENT_FREE_RADICAL_GATE=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Homogeneous quadratic GCD adapter


For every primitive positive physical endpoint set
  P = [e:R:x:y] in P^3(Q).


Because gcd(e,x,y)=1, these four integral coordinates are primitive. Also
  R^2=e^2+x^2+y^2
gives
  max(e,R,x,y)=R
on the positive chamber, so the standard projective height is
  H(P)=R,
  h(P)=log R.


Define the two homogeneous quadratic forms
  F1 = eR,
  F2 = xy.
Then exactly
  G_* = gcd(F1(P),F2(P)).                           (229O.9)


Thus the remaining 229N obstruction is now an exact squarefree-kernel tail for the GCD of two degree-2 homogeneous forms at a highly constrained physical subset of primitive P^3(Q), with the ambient projective height identical to the Stage37 physical height R.


RESULT_229O_HOMOGENEOUS_QUADRATIC_GCD_ADAPTER=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229O_AMBIENT_HEIGHT_EQUALS_PHYSICAL_R=true.


This is a theorem-input simplification only. The physical points still lie on the retained simultaneous Pythagorean/square conditions, and no ambient-P^3 density statement may be substituted for the exact physical population.


5. Yasufuku 2026 codimension-2 GCD inequality: direct route is closed


Yu Yasufuku, “GCD inequalities arising from codimension-2 blowups,” Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 58(4), 2026, DOI 10.1112/blms.70349, gives an unconditional codimension-2 GCD inequality for two homogeneous forms.


For the 229O ambient adapter:
  n=3,
  d1=d2=2,
  F1=eR,
  F2=xy.


The center
  Y={eR=xy=0}
is a codimension-2 complete intersection because F1 and F2 have no common polynomial factor. However Yasufuku Theorem 1.2 also requires every coordinate point of P^3 to lie outside Y. Here every coordinate point has eR=0 and xy=0, hence every coordinate point lies in Y.


Therefore the theorem is not directly applicable to (F1,F2).


Moreover, even if this coordinate-point hypothesis were ignored, the equal-degree coefficient allowed by Yasufuku is any number larger than
  [-(n+1)-(n-1)d
   +sqrt((n+1)^2 d^2+2(n^2-1)d+(n+1)^2)]/2.
At n=3,d=2 this equals
  (-8+sqrt(112))/2
  = 2 sqrt(7)-4
  = 1.2915... .


Stage37 requires control at the B^(1/3-delta) radical scale. A pointwise logarithmic GCD coefficient already exceeding 1.29, before Yasufuku's additional nonnegative coordinate-boundary term, cannot provide that receiver.


RESULT_229O_YASUFUKU_2026_DIRECT_MATCH=NO_GO.
NO_GO_REASON_1=coordinate-point hypothesis fails maximally.
NO_GO_REASON_2=even counterfactual main coefficient 2sqrt(7)-4 > 1/3.


6. Barrios 2026 corrected generalized-GCD theorem: componentwise route is also too weak


Benjamín Barrios, “An upper bound for the generalized greatest common divisor of rational points,” together with the published 2026 correction, gives a generalized GCD height bound outside a proper Zariski-closed exceptional set. The correction states that the height-bound results remain valid after adding the requirement that the relevant subvariety have ample normal bundle.


The reducible center Y={eR=xy=0} is the union of four coordinate lines
  Y_ex={e=x=0},
  Y_ey={e=y=0},
  Y_Rx={R=x=0},
  Y_Ry={R=y=0}.


Each component is a smooth line P^1 in P^3 and has ample normal bundle
  N_{P^1/P^3}=O(1) direct-sum O(1).
So the corrected Barrios theorem is eligible componentwise.


For X=P^3, A=O(1), n=3, a line has d=1 and codimension c=2, while
  (A^d . Y)=1,
  (A^n)=1.
The theorem's coefficient is therefore
  [(1/1)*(3!/2!)]^(1/2)
   = sqrt(3)
   = 1.732...                                      (229O.10)
plus epsilon.


Thus even for one bucket such as gcd(e,x), the black-box pointwise bound is far above the 1/3 exponent scale needed by Stage37. Applying the theorem separately to four line components does not improve this exponent, and the theorem also excludes a proper Zariski-closed exceptional set whose intersection with the physical locus would require a separate count.


RESULT_229O_BARRIOS_2026_COMPONENTWISE_MATCH=NO_GO_FOR_STAGE37_BUDGET.
NO_GO_REASON=eligible after correction, but coefficient sqrt(3)>1/3 and exceptional-set count remains separate.


7. Consequence for the current research gate


The exact preferred gate after 229O is


PHYSICAL_JOINT_RADICAL_GCD_ONE_THIRD_QUOTIENT_FREE:
for some fixed delta>0,
  # {primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B:
       sf(gcd(eR,xy)) > B^(1/3-delta)}
     = o(B^(1/3)).                                (229O.11)


Together with 229L/229N this is sufficient for the full endpoint numerator:
  P(B)
   <= #large-radical-tail
      + B^(1/3-delta+o(1)).


229O removes an algebraic nuisance in the theorem interface but does not improve the endpoint exponent. The current 2026 ambient GCD-height black boxes inspected above do not meet the receiver.


The next legal theorem input must exploit additional structure absent from ambient P^3 GCD inequalities, for example:
- the exact physical simultaneous Pythagorean/square locus;
- squarefree radical support rather than raw GCD size;
- an average/counting theorem rather than a pointwise height inequality;
- or a stronger sufficient raw branch that meets the same B^(1/3) budget on the exact physical measure.


Do not next:
- reinsert the quotient xy/gcd(x,y)^2;
- treat Yasufuku 2026 as applicable despite its coordinate-point hypothesis;
- use Barrios componentwise bounds as a power saving;
- infer the radical tail from a raw pointwise GCD height bound with exponent >1/3;
- discard the exceptional Zariski set without a physical count;
- restart generic gcd heuristics, fixed-d/Kummer, LOCAL, PAIR, A, or FIB without a new matching quantitative input.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_GENUINELY_NEW_THEOREM_INPUT.


8. Sources checked


Internal:
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229N;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229M;
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229D;
- M3-T11-228;
- current MAIN / RESULT-LEDGER / CARD-INDEX / active ROUTE.


External:
- Yu Yasufuku, “GCD inequalities arising from codimension-2 blowups,” Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 58(4) (2026), DOI 10.1112/blms.70349.
- Benjamín Barrios, “An upper bound for the generalized greatest common divisor of rational points,” arXiv:2411.06050 / Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society.
- Benjamín Barrios, correction published online 22 July 2026, DOI 10.1017/S0004972726101543.


AUDIT SCOPE


This card proves an exact physical quotient-removal identity and performs a scoped current-theorem contract audit. It is not an independent hostile audit of cards 186–229. It gives no global P(B)/M3(B) limit and no perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion.

records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229N — single physical radical-gcd receiver for the full twist support


STATUS: POST_229M_SINGLE_GCD_COLLAPSE_COMPLETE / PROVED_CRAW_EQUALS_GCD_R_CF / PROVED_AEDGE_EQUALS_GCD_E_XPRIMEYPRIME / PROVED_TWIST_CONTENT_EQUALS_SINGLE_PHYSICAL_GCD / PROVED_FOUR_BUCKET_GCD_MATRIX / PROVED_SMALL_RADICAL_GCD_SECTOR_o_M3 / TWO_RAW_TAILS_SUPERSEDED_AS_PREFERRED_GATE / LARGE_RADICAL_GCD_TAIL_OPEN / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229M EXACT GCD COLLAPSE / SINGLE SQUAREFREE-KERNEL RECEIVER / FULL-ENDPOINT SCOPED COUNT / ANTI-LOOP FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229M
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229M proved for every positive physical endpoint
  d = sf(2^epsilon A_edge C_raw),
where
  A_edge = a b = gcd(e,xy),
  C_raw  = c12 c21,
and a,b,c12,c21 are four pairwise-coprime physical Pythagorean contents.


229M then used raw thresholds on A_edge and C_raw. That is sufficient but not optimal, because the 229L fixed-d theorem only sees the squarefree twist class. Large square parts of A_edge or C_raw do not create new d.


This card collapses the two raw content variables to one exact physical gcd and replaces the two-tail target by one squarefree-kernel tail.


2. Normalize the missing-face triple


Retain 229D notation:
  d0 = gcd(x,y),
  x = d0 b c,
  y = d0 a f,
with
  gcd(bc,af)=1.
Define
  x' = x/d0 = b c,
  y' = y/d0 = a f.
Then
  gcd(x',y')=1
and
  x'^2+y'^2=q^2
is the primitive missing-face Pythagorean triple.


Also retain
  e = g a b,
with
  gcd(g,c)=gcd(g,f)=1.


3. A_edge is exactly gcd(e,x'y')


Since
  x'y' = a b c f,
we have
  gcd(e,x'y')
    = gcd(gab,abcf)
    = ab gcd(g,cf)
    = ab.
Therefore
  A_edge = gcd(e,x'y').                          (229N.1)


RESULT_229N_AEDGE_SINGLE_GCD=PROVED_EXACT.


4. The two space contents are exactly gcd(R,f) and gcd(R,c)


Recall
  c12 = gcd(U,y),
  c21 = gcd(V,x),
with
  c12|f,
  c21|c.


First prove
  gcd(R,f)=c12.
The inclusion c12|R follows because c12 divides both U and y and
  R^2=U^2+y^2.
Also c12|f by 229M.


Conversely let r divide both R and f. Since f|y, r|y. Then
  U^2=R^2-y^2
is divisible by r^2, so r|U. Thus
  r|gcd(U,y)=c12.
Hence gcd(R,f)=c12.


Identically,
  gcd(R,c)=c21.                                  (229N.2)


Since gcd(c,f)=1,
  gcd(R,cf)
   = gcd(R,c) gcd(R,f)
   = c21 c12
   = C_raw.                                      (229N.3)


RESULT_229N_CRAW_EQUALS_GCD_R_CF=PROVED_EXACT.


5. C_raw is exactly gcd(R,x'y')


We need to remove the factors a,b from x'y'=abcf.


If a prime divides R and a, then it divides R,e,y because a|e and a|y. The sphere equation
  R^2=e^2+x^2+y^2
then forces that prime to divide x, contradicting the primitive physical condition
  gcd(e,x,y)=1.
Therefore
  gcd(R,a)=1.
Similarly
  gcd(R,b)=1.


Hence
  gcd(R,x'y')
   = gcd(R,abcf)
   = gcd(R,cf)
   = C_raw.                                      (229N.4)


RESULT_229N_CRAW_SINGLE_GCD=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Exact single-gcd collapse


Define the physical joint gcd
  G_* := gcd(eR,x'y').                           (229N.5)


No prime dividing x'y' can divide both e and R: if p|e,R and p divides x' or y', then p divides one of x,y, and the sphere equation forces p to divide the other edge as well, contradicting gcd(e,x,y)=1.


Therefore the e-side and R-side gcds with x'y' are coprime, and
  G_*
   = gcd(e,x'y') gcd(R,x'y')
   = A_edge C_raw.                               (229N.6)


Combining with 229M,
  d = sf(2^epsilon G_*).                         (229N.7)


Equivalently,
  G_* = gcd(eR, (xy)/gcd(x,y)^2).                (229N.8)


This is the exact whole-endpoint twist-support receiver.


RESULT_229N_TWIST_CONTENT_EQUALS_SINGLE_PHYSICAL_GCD=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229N_TWIST_CLASS_SINGLE_GCD=d_EQ_sf_2EPS_GSTAR.
RESULT_229N_TWO_RAW_CONTENT_VARIABLES_COLLAPSE_TO_ONE=true.


7. Exact four-bucket gcd matrix


The same argument gives the four entries directly:
  gcd(e,x') = b,
  gcd(e,y') = a,
  gcd(R,x') = c21,
  gcd(R,y') = c12.                               (229N.9)


They are pairwise coprime by 229M. Hence every odd prime divisor of G_* lies in exactly one physical bucket in the 2x2 matrix


             x'      y'
    e        b       a
    R        c21     c12


and no prime is double-charged across buckets.


This is a stronger bookkeeping statement than the raw two-tail split. The twist support is exactly the squarefree support of this one four-bucket gcd matrix, up to the single 2-adic bit epsilon.


RESULT_229N_FOUR_BUCKET_GCD_MATRIX=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229N_NO_ODD_PRIME_DOUBLE_CHARGE=true.


8. Replace raw size by the actual squarefree kernel


Define
  K_*(E) := sf(G_*(E))
for a physical endpoint E.


From (229N.7), d differs from K_* only in the 2-adic bit. In particular
  d <= 2 K_*,
and for a fixed value of K_* there are at most two possible canonical d.


Let delta>0 be fixed. On the sector
  K_* <= B^(1/3-delta),                         (229N.10)

  O(B^(1/3-delta)).

  # {E:R<=B, K_*(E)<=B^(1/3-delta)}
    <= B^(1/3-delta+o(1))

where
  P_rad-tail(B)
   := # {E:R<=B, sf(gcd(eR,xy/gcd(x,y)^2))

  A_edge <= B^alpha,
  C_raw  <= B^beta,

  K_* = sf(A_edge C_raw)
       <= A_edge C_raw
       <= B^(alpha+beta),

But the converse can fail badly: A_edge or C_raw may be large because of square factors while K_* is small. Such endpoints are already absorbed by the fixed-d B^{o(1)} theorem and do not belong in the true moving-support obstruction.

RESULT_229N_229M_TWO_RAW_TAILS=SUPERSEDED_AS_PREFERRED_GATE_ONLY.
No 229M theorem is retracted.


10. New exact restart contract


The Gaussian/twist route now needs only one quantitative theorem:


PHYSICAL_JOINT_RADICAL_GCD_ONE_THIRD:
for some fixed delta>0,
  # {primitive positive physical endpoints R<=B:

     = o(B^(1/3)).                               (229N.14)

Likewise generic logarithmic-gcd and semiabelian gcd theorems are not an exact counting theorem for this occupied physical family.

﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229M — twist class as four physical Pythagorean contents and complementary one-sixth tail reduction


STATUS: POST_229L_CONTENT_CROSSWALK_COMPLETE / PROVED_EXPLICIT_HILBERT_CLASS_FORMULA / PROVED_TWIST_CLASS_FOUR_PHYSICAL_CONTENTS / PROVED_PAIRWISE_COPRIME_CONTENT_SUPPORT / PROVED_TWIST_CONTENT_PRODUCT_IDENTITY / PROVED_SMALL_SMALL_CONTENT_SECTOR_o_M3 / PROVED_COMPLEMENTARY_ONE_SIXTH_TWO_TAIL_REDUCTION / MOVING_LARGE_CONTENT_TAILS_OPEN / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229L EXACT CONTENT CROSSWALK / PYTHAGOREAN GAP SQUARECLASSES / GAUSSIAN-TWIST TO CROSS-GCD ROUTER / SCOPED ENDPOINT SECTOR DISPOSAL / ANTI-LOOP FIREWALL


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229L
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229L reduced the full positive physical endpoint count to a moving congruent-number twist support:
  P(B) <= T_tw(B) B^{o(1)},
where T_tw(B) counts canonical positive squarefree twist classes d realized by
  E_d: Y^2=X^3-d^2 X.
The fixed-d fiber is uniformly B^{o(1)}.


The remaining question is whether d is a genuinely new moving parameter or is already encoded by retained Stage37 physical contents. This card gives the exact answer: d is the squarefree kernel of four existing physical Pythagorean triangle contents, up to one 2-adic parity bit.


Notation on the 229F/229J physical chart:
  x^2+y^2=z^2,
  e^2+z^2=R^2,
  U^2=e^2+x^2,
  V^2=e^2+y^2,
with all x,y,z,e,U,V,R positive and R<=B.


2. Explicit rational squareclass representative for a norm-square element


LEMMA 229M.1.
Let K=Q(i), let zeta in K^* be non-real, and suppose
  N(zeta)=r^2
with r in Q_{>0}.
Then the rational squareclass in the Hilbert-90 descent of 229L may be represented by
  2r+Tr(zeta).


Proof.
Set
  w=r+zeta.
Since zeta is non-real, w is nonzero. From zeta*conj(zeta)=r^2,
  zeta/r = (r+zeta)/(r+conj(zeta)) = w/conj(w).
Hence
  zeta = [r/N(w)] w^2.
But
  N(w)=r(2r+Tr(zeta)),
so the rational coefficient is
  1/(2r+Tr(zeta)).
An element and its inverse have the same class in Q^*/Q^{*2}, proving the claim.


RESULT_229M_EXPLICIT_HILBERT_CLASS=PROVED_EXACT.


For the positive physical p of 229J, both p^2+1 and p^2-1 are non-real because p has positive real and imaginary parts, so the lemma applies without an exceptional real branch.


3. The two selector squareclasses are physical diagonal-gap products


Retain 229J:
  p=u v,
  q=conj(p),
  v=(R+e)/z,
and normalized coordinates
  X0=x/z, Y0=y/z, T=e/z, S=R/z,
  U0=U/z, V0=V/z.


For
  zeta_+=p^2+1,
229J gives
  sqrt(N(zeta_+)) = 2 v U0.
A direct calculation using
  X0^2+Y0^2=1,
  U0^2=T^2+X0^2,
  S=(v+v^{-1})/2,
  T=(v-v^{-1})/2
gives
  2 sqrt(N(zeta_+)) + Tr(zeta_+)
    =4 v^2 (U0-T)(U0+S).


The factor 4v^2 is a rational square and z^{-2} is a rational square, therefore the 229L rational squareclass delta_+ satisfies
  [delta_+]
    =[(U-e)(U+R)]
    =[(U-e)(R-U)],                              (229M.1)
because
  (U+R)(R-U)=R^2-U^2=y^2.


Similarly, for
  zeta_-=p^2-1,
229J gives
  sqrt(N(zeta_-)) = 2 v V0,
and
  2 sqrt(N(zeta_-)) + Tr(zeta_-)
    =4 v^2 (S-V0)(T+V0).
Hence
  [delta_-]
    =[(R-V)(V+e)]
    =[(R-V)(V-e)],                              (229M.2)
because
  (V+e)(V-e)=V^2-e^2=y^2.


Thus the 229L twist squareclass D=delta_+ delta_- satisfies
  [D]
   =[(U-e)(R-U)(V-e)(R-V)].                    (229M.3)


RESULT_229M_SELECTOR_CLASSES_AS_PHYSICAL_GAPS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229M_TWIST_CLASS_AS_FOUR_DIAGONAL_GAPS=PROVED_EXACT.


4. Elementary Pythagorean content-squareclass lemma


LEMMA 229M.2.
Let
  A^2+B^2=C^2
be a positive integral Pythagorean triple with content
  c=gcd(A,B)=gcd(A,B,C).
Write A=c A0, B=c B0, C=c C0 with the primitive triple (A0,B0,C0).
Then
  [C-A]=[c]        if A0 is even,
  [C-A]=[2c]       if A0 is odd
in Q^*/Q^{*2}.


Proof.
For a primitive triple:
- if A0 is the even leg, A0=2mn and C0-A0=(m-n)^2;
- if A0 is the odd leg, A0=m^2-n^2 and C0-A0=2n^2.
Multiplying by c proves the claim.


5. Exact twist class equals four existing physical triangle contents


Define the four physical Pythagorean contents
  b   = gcd(e,x)   for (e,x,U),
  c12 = gcd(U,y)   for (U,y,R),
  a   = gcd(e,y)   for (e,y,V),
  c21 = gcd(V,x)   for (V,x,R).                 (229M.4)


The first two pairwise edge contents are exactly 229D:
  gcd(e,x)=b,
  gcd(e,y)=a.
The last two are exactly the two space-triangle contents of M3-XG-007.


Apply Lemma 229M.2 to the four triples
  (e,x,U),
  (U,y,R),
  (e,y,V),
  (V,x,R)
and use (229M.1)-(229M.3). There is a parity bit
  epsilon in {0,1}
determined by the four primitive leg orientations such that
  [D]=[2^epsilon a b c12 c21].                 (229M.5)


Therefore the canonical positive squarefree twist class of 229L is exactly
  d = sf(2^epsilon a b c12 c21).               (229M.6)


No Gaussian prime outside these four physical contents can enter the rational twist support.


RESULT_229M_TWIST_CLASS_FOUR_PHYSICAL_CONTENTS=PROVED_EXACT.


6. Pairwise coprimality and four-chart realization


Use 229D:
  L1=g a, L2=g b,
  M1=d0 c, M2=d0 f,
with
  e=gab, x=d0 bc, y=d0 af,
and primitive face triples
  (ga, d0 c, n1),
  (gb, d0 f, n2).


From M3-T11-228 the physical face diagonals are
  U=b n1,
  V=a n2.


Because gcd(b,d0 a f)=1 and n1 is coprime to both legs ga,d0c,
  c12=gcd(U,y)
      =gcd(b n1,d0 a f)
      =gcd(n1,f).                                (229M.7)
Thus c12|f and gcd(c12,ab)=1.


Similarly
  c21=gcd(V,x)
      =gcd(a n2,d0 b c)
      =gcd(n2,c),                                (229M.8)
so c21|c and gcd(c21,ab)=1.


Since gcd(c,f)=1,
  gcd(c12,c21)=1.
Together with gcd(a,b)=1, the four contents
  a,b,c12,c21
are pairwise coprime.


In particular the odd-prime support of d is the disjoint union of the odd-prime squarefree supports of these four physical contents. There is no cancellation between separate content buckets.


RESULT_229M_FOUR_CONTENTS_PAIRWISE_COPRIME=PROVED_EXACT.


7. Collapse to two retained moving content products


Define
  A_edge := a b,
  C_raw  := c12 c21.


By 229D,
  A_edge=ab=e/g.
Because gcd(e,x,y)=1 and a=gcd(e,y), b=gcd(e,x), one also has exactly
  A_edge=gcd(e,xy).                              (229M.9)


By M3-XG-007,
  C_raw=c12 c21
is the existing raw cross-gcd / product of the two coprime space-triangle contents, and there is an integer t>=1 with
  R=C_raw t.                                     (229M.10)


Hence
  C_tw := a b c12 c21
        = A_edge C_raw
        = (e/g) C_raw
        = eR/(g t).                              (229M.11)


The twist class satisfies
  d=sf(2^epsilon C_tw),
so in particular
  d <= 2 C_tw <= 2 e R <= 2 B^2.                (229M.12)


This sharpens 229L's coarse d<=B^{O(1)} height statement to an explicit quadratic bound, but B^2 by itself is far above the Stage37 support target.


RESULT_229M_TWIST_CONTENT_PRODUCT=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229M_A_EDGE_EQUALS_GCD_E_XY=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229M_CTW_EQUALS_AEDGE_TIMES_CRAW=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229M_TWIST_SIZE_D_LE_2B2=PROVED.


8. New scoped counting theorem: the small-small content sector is negligible


Let alpha,beta>0 with
  alpha+beta < 1/3.
Consider full positive physical endpoints satisfying
  A_edge <= B^alpha,
  C_raw  <= B^beta.                              (229M.13)


By (229M.6)/(229M.11),
  d <= 2 B^{alpha+beta}.
Thus the number of possible positive squarefree twist classes in this sector is
  O(B^{alpha+beta}).


By the 229L uniform fixed-d endpoint fiber theorem, each such d contributes
  B^{o(1)}
physical endpoints, uniformly in d. Therefore
  # endpoints satisfying (229M.13)
    <= B^{alpha+beta+o(1)}
    = o(B^{1/3}).                                (229M.14)


Since the retained denominator lower bound is
  M3(B) >> B^{1/3},
this entire sector is o(M3).


RESULT_229M_SMALL_SMALL_CONTENT_SECTOR=o_M3.
RESULT_229M_SMALL_SMALL_CONTENT_SECTOR_ENDPOINT_BOUND=B^{alpha+beta+o(1)}.


This is genuine new scoped counting credit, but it is not a full numerator bound and does not change GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT from 0.


9. Complementary one-sixth two-tail reduction


The most useful specialization preserves the existing CROSS-GCD useful threshold.


Choose
  0<xi<1/12
and a fixed eta>0 small enough that
  alpha = 1/6-xi-2eta >0,
  beta  = 1/6+xi.
Then
  alpha+beta = 1/3-2eta.


By Section 8, endpoints outside the union
  A_edge > B^(1/6-xi-2eta),                     (A-tail)
or
  C_raw  > B^(1/6+xi)                           (C-tail)
contribute only
  O(B^(1/3-2eta+o(1)))=o(M3).                   (229M.15)


Equivalently,
  P(B)
   <= P_A-tail(B)
      + P_C-tail(B)
      + B^(1/3-2eta+o(1)).                       (229M.16)


The C-tail is exactly the retained useful-threshold raw cross-gcd problem emphasized after M3-T11-156:
  C_raw > B^(1/6+xi).
The A-tail is the complementary pairwise-edge-content product problem
  A_edge=ab=gcd(e,xy)>B^(1/6-xi-2eta).


RESULT_229M_COMPLEMENTARY_ONE_SIXTH_TWO_TAIL_REDUCTION=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229M_C_TAIL_IS_EXISTING_CROSS_GCD_USEFUL_THRESHOLD=true.
RESULT_229M_A_TAIL_IS_PAIRWISE_EDGE_CONTENT_PRODUCT_THRESHOLD=true.


10. Route consequences and anti-loop firewall


The 229L moving twist support is NOT an independent fifth mechanism after this card.


Its exact arithmetic support is already the squarefree kernel of
  A_edge*C_raw,
where
- A_edge is the 229D pairwise physical edge-content product;
- C_raw is the M3-XG-007 / CROSS-GCD product of the two physical space-triangle contents.


Therefore a future proof of either of the following would close the Gaussian/twist route after the complementary sector split:
- both large-content tails in (229M.15) are o(B^{1/3});
- a direct same-measure joint theorem for occupied (A_edge,C_raw) squarefree-kernel support gives o(B^{1/3});
- a stronger theorem controls the union in (229M.15) directly.


What does NOT suffice:
- another fixed-d point count;
- another proof that E_d is a congruent-number twist;
- generic Selmer-density information not transferred to the exact physical occupied support;
- independent multiplication of a CROSS-GCD saving and an A_edge saving without a same-measure union/joint theorem.


The existing 156 firewall remains: a uniform raw 1/C tail is false on the enlarged carrier; the useful threshold C_raw>B^(1/6+xi) was not refuted but is still unproved. The A_edge complementary tail is likewise currently unproved.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.

11. Current theorem rematch


A targeted literature scan after 229L found work on integral points and 2-descent in the congruent-number family, including Chan–Zhang's uniform/coset bounds for integral points. Those results control point multiplicity inside a fixed twist family or average integral-point counts; they do not bound the number of Stage37-realized twist classes, nor the exact physical large-content tails in (229M.15).


Santens 2026 still supplies the non-split toric base/fixed-local framework but not a growing-gcd/level-of-distribution theorem for A_edge or C_raw. Huang's effective toric geometric sieve remains split-over-Q. Thus no inspected theorem closes either large tail on the exact physical measure.


RESULT_229M_CURRENT_EXTERNAL_THEOREM_MATCH=NO_DIRECT_LARGE_CONTENT_TAIL_BOUND.


12. Next legal research target


Do not continue Gaussian norm identities or fixed-d elliptic geometry.


The next exact target is now one of:


(A) A_EDGE_LARGE_TAIL:
  # {endpoint: gcd(e,xy)>B^(1/6-xi-2eta)}

with

  N(p^2-1) in Q^{*2},
and exact physical projective height inherited from
  p=((x+i y)(R+e))/z^2
on [x:y:z:e:R] with R<=B.

The current card does not extend the toric identity chain. It converts the Gaussian norm-square conditions into a moving family of elliptic curves to which a current uniform bounded-height theorem applies.


For the physical positive population p is automatically nonzero. The apparent selector boundaries p^2=+-1 are treated exactly in Section 4 and are physically empty; thus the router below covers the full positive physical endpoint population.


2. Hilbert-90 squareclass descent lemma over Q(i)


LEMMA 229L.1.
Let z in K^* with K=Q(i). If
  N_{K/Q}(z)=r^2
for some r in Q^*, then the K-squareclass of z comes from a rational squareclass:
  z = delta * w^2
for some delta in Q^* and w in K^*.


Proof.
Put xi=z/r. Then N(xi)=1. By Hilbert 90 there is w in K^* such that
  xi=w/conj(w).
But
  w/conj(w)=w^2/N(w),
and N(w) is rational. Hence
  z=(r/N(w))*w^2.
Take delta=r/N(w) in Q^*. QED.


The rational squareclass is unique only modulo the kernel of
  Q^*/Q^{*2} -> K^*/K^{*2};
for K=Q(i), the sign class disappears because -1=i^2. We therefore use a positive squarefree integer representative whenever a canonical rational representative is needed.


RESULT_229L_NORM_SQUARECLASS_DESCENT=PROVED_EXACT.


3. Apply the lemma to the 229J Gaussian norm triple


For every nondegenerate 229J selector point there exist
  delta_0, delta_+, delta_- in Q^*
and
  c,a,b in K^*
such that
  p       = delta_0 c^2,
  p^2+1   = delta_+ a^2,
  p^2-1   = delta_- b^2.                       (229L.1)


The first identity is equivalent to the base condition N(p) square at the squareclass level. The second and third are the two endpoint selector conditions.


Put
  D = delta_+ delta_-.
Multiplying the last two equations gives
  p^4-1 = D (ab)^2.                             (229L.2)


The squareclass [D] in Q^*/(Q^{*2}*{+-1}) is canonically determined by p; changing delta_+ or delta_- by the sign kernel does not affect the elliptic curve below because only D^2 occurs.


RESULT_229L_GAUSSIAN_TRIPLE_TO_RATIONAL_TWIST_CLASS=PROVED.


4. Exact congruent-number elliptic twist router


Define
  X_E = D p^2,
  Y_E = D^2 p a b.


Using (229L.2),
  Y_E^2
    = D^4 p^2 a^2 b^2
    = D^3 p^2(p^4-1)
    = X_E^3-D^2 X_E.


Thus every nondegenerate Gaussian norm-triple point maps to
  E_D: Y^2=X^3-D^2 X                              (229L.3)
over K=Q(i).


This is the standard congruent-number quadratic-twist family, now used only as an exact Stage37 router. E_D has the K-rational 2-torsion points
  (0,0), (D,0), (-D,0).


The original two selector squareclasses are visible on E_D:
  X_E+D
    = D(p^2+1)
    = delta_- (delta_+ a)^2,
  X_E-D
    = D(p^2-1)
    = delta_+ (delta_- b)^2,
and
  X_E/D=p^2 is a K-square.                        (229L.4)


Therefore the image lies in a distinguished 2-descent class of E_D, and the individual rational squareclasses delta_+,delta_- are recoverable from [X_E-D] and [X_E+D] in K^*/K^{*2}, up to the harmless rational sign kernel.


There is also no hidden moving multiplicity from physical endpoints to p. For a Q-rational base point q=conj(p), while p=uv and q=v/u, hence v^2=pq=N(p). On the positive physical chamber v=(R+e)/z>0, so v is the unique positive rational square root of N(p), then u=p/v. The inverse formulas of 229J recover X/Z,Y/Z,S/Z,T/Z uniquely from u,v, and the primitive positive representative is unique. Thus a physical endpoint determines p injectively.


For fixed canonical twist class d, X_E/d=p^2 determines p up to sign from the elliptic point; the physical first-quadrant condition selects the physical sign. Hence the endpoint-to-E_d router has O(1) (indeed physical-sign-one) multiplicity.


Finally, the apparent excluded values are physically impossible. If p^2=1 then q=p, so u^2=p/q=1 and Y/Z=(u-u^(-1))/(2i)=0, hence y=0. If p^2=-1 then q=-p, so u^2=p/q=-1 and X/Z=(u+u^(-1))/2=0, hence x=0. Both contradict positive physical edges. Therefore no endpoint boundary term remains.


RESULT_229L_CONGRUENT_NUMBER_TWIST_ROUTER=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229L_DISTINGUISHED_2_DESCENT_LABELS=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229L_FIXED_TWIST_ROUTER_MULTIPLICITY=O(1).


5. Coarse physical-height control of the twist and elliptic point


On the exact 229J physical chart
  p=((x+i y)(R+e))/z^2,
with positive integral physical coordinates bounded by R<=B.


Hence the logarithmic Weil height satisfies
  h_K(p)=O(log B).                                (229L.5)


The K-squareclass of p^4-1 may be represented by a positive squarefree rational integer d. Indeed the denominator z^8 is already a square, while every rational prime occurring in d lies below a prime divisor of the Gaussian integer numerator
  ((x+i y)(R+e))^4-z^8.
Its norm is B^{O(1)}. Therefore one may choose the canonical squarefree representative with
  |d| <= B^{O(1)},
equivalently
  log |d|=O(log B).                               (229L.6)


After replacing D by this canonical representative, E_D is Q-isomorphic over K to E_d by a rational square scaling. The corresponding elliptic point has
  h(P_d)=O(log B),                                (229L.7)
so its exponential projective height is at most B^C for some absolute fixed C on this Stage37 chart.


This is deliberately only a coarse polynomial-height adapter. No optimal exponent or leading constant is claimed.


RESULT_229L_TWIST_CONDUCTOR_POLYNOMIAL_HEIGHT=PROVED_COARSE.
RESULT_229L_ELLIPTIC_POINT_HEIGHT_POLYNOMIAL_IN_PHYSICAL_B=PROVED_COARSE.


6. Dujella 2025 gives a uniform fixed-twist fiber bound


Marta Dujella, “Uniform bounds for the number of rational points of bounded height on certain elliptic curves,” Acta Arithmetica 217 (2025), 309–332, DOI 10.4064/aa231221-9-10, proves the following theorem species:


For an elliptic curve E over a fixed number field k having a k-rational point of exact prime order ell, the number of E(k) points of exponential height at most H is at most
  exp(C(k) log H / log log H),
with effective constant depending only on k.


Apply this with
  k=Q(i), ell=2,
to every E_d in (229L.3). The curves E_d all have rational 2-torsion, and the constant is uniform in the twist d.


Together with (229L.7), for every canonical twist class d,
  # {Stage37 Gaussian norm-triple points with R<=B and twist d}
      <= B^{o(1)},                                (229L.8)
uniformly in d.


This counts all K-rational points on E_d, so the distinguished 2-descent restriction can only reduce the count. The O(1) router multiplicity has no effect.


RESULT_229L_UNIFORM_FIXED_TWIST_ENDPOINT_FIBER=B^{o(1)}.
RESULT_229L_DUJELLA_THEOREM_MATCH=APPLIES_TO_FIXED_TWIST_FIBER_UNIFORMLY_IN_d.


7. New exact whole-numerator receiver


Let
  T_tw(B)
be the number of canonical positive squarefree twist classes d realized by physical endpoint points of height R<=B through the router above.


Partitioning the endpoint population by d and using (229L.8) gives
  P(B) <= T_tw(B) B^{o(1)},                       (229L.9)
for the full positive physical endpoint count P(B).


Therefore the exact new sufficient receiver is
  T_tw(B) = o(B^{1/3})                             (229L.10)
for absolute numerator closure on this dense open, because M3(B)>>B^{1/3} is retained.


More generally any fixed-power estimate
  T_tw(B) << B^{1/3-epsilon}
closes the full endpoint numerator with room.


This receiver is different from PAIR's weighted w=D/X image and from LOCAL's fixed-Q M3 residue contraction. It is an endpoint-defined moving quadratic-twist support count obtained after the exact Gaussian norm-triple adapter.


RESULT_229L_MOVING_TWIST_SUPPORT_RECEIVER=PROVED_EXACT.
RESULT_229L_FIXED_TWIST_POINT_COUNT_NO_LONGER_BLOCKER=true.
RESULT_229L_PHYSICAL_SELECTOR_BOUNDARY=EMPTY_EXACT.
RESULT_229L_ENDPOINT_TO_P_MULTIPLICITY=1_ON_POSITIVE_PHYSICAL_CHAMBER.
RESULT_229L_REMAINING_GAUSSIAN_BLOCKER=MOVING_TWIST_SUPPORT_COUNT.


8. Current theorem rematch and nontransfer checks


Phillips 2026 gives asymptotics, often with power-saving error, for bounded-height points in the domain of morphisms of weighted projective stacks, including possibly infinite local conditions. This is a strong current theorem species, but no exact finite-defect morphism from the Stage37 moving twist-support space or the 229J K3 selector surface to the required weighted-projective-stack source is currently established. Therefore it does not presently bound T_tw(B).


The old Stage37 quadratic-twist and 2-descent cards located by CARD-INDEX (including M3-T11-053, M3-T11-103, M3-DESC-NEG-001 and M3-T11-081) concern different singular/fixed-squareclass carriers. None states the 229J Gaussian norm-triple -> moving congruent-number twist router or the uniform fixed-twist fiber bound (229L.8). No supersession or retraction of those scoped results is implied.


No theorem found in the current rematch bounds the number of realized d strongly enough for (229L.10).


9. What changed and what did not


Changed:
- the Gaussian norm-square condition is no longer only a Kummer/K3 geometry target;
- every nondegenerate selector point has a canonical moving congruent-number twist class;
- for each fixed twist class, the entire endpoint fiber is uniformly B^{o(1)};
- the quantitative geometry blocker is sharpened from “count the Gaussian norm triple” to “count the realized moving twist support T_tw(B)”; the apparent p^2=+-1 boundary is exactly empty on the positive physical population.


Not changed:
- T_tw(B)=o(B^{1/3}) is not proved;
- no global endpoint exponent improves yet;
- no exact-M3 LOCAL, PAIR, A or FIB receiver is supplied;
- there is no remaining selector-boundary count: p=0 is outside the torus and p^2=+-1 forces x=0 or y=0, impossible physically;
- no perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence conclusion follows.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
GEOMETRY_REOPEN=false.
LOCAL_REOPEN=false.
PAIR_REOPEN=false.
A_REOPEN=false.
FIB_REOPEN=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_GENUINELY_NEW_THEOREM_INPUT.


10. Sharpened next theorem watch


Highest-value Gaussian route input is now:


(A) MOVING_CONGRUENT_TWIST_SUPPORT:
prove
  T_tw(B)=o(B^{1/3}),
or a stronger fixed-power bound, for twist classes d actually realized by the 229J physical chart with both selector conditions;


(B) TWIST-SUPPORT SIEVE / SELMER SUPPORT:
a theorem bounding the number of squarefree d for which E_d(Q(i)) contains a point in the distinguished 2-descent image (229L.4) with the inherited physical-height restrictions;


(C) DIRECT GAUSSIAN/K3 COUNT:
a direct theorem that bypasses twist support but implies (229L.9) with sufficient exponent.


Dujella removes the fixed-twist rational-point multiplicity as a primary obstruction, and the physical selector boundary is empty. Do not spend another production card reproving fixed-d finiteness or generic Kummer structure. The next useful move must control moving d-support.


11. Sources checked


- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229J.
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229K.
- M3-GOAL-001.
- CARD-INDEX searches for quadratic twist / Kummer / CM elliptic / Gaussian norm triple / 2-descent.
- Marta Dujella, Acta Arithmetica 217 (2025), 309–332, DOI 10.4064/aa231221-9-10.
- Tristan Phillips, Journal of the London Mathematical Society 113 (2026), e70486, DOI 10.1112/jlms.70486.


AUDIT SCOPE


This is an exact algebraic adapter, coarse exact-height comparison, and current-theorem applicability audit. It is not an independent hostile audit of cards 186–229. No global counting credit, perfect-cuboid conclusion, or T11-230 production issuance is claimed.

records.title: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229K — Santens nonsplit fixed-local toric rematch and certified degree-four selector cover
records.content:
﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229K — Santens nonsplit fixed-local toric rematch and certified degree-four selector cover


STATUS: POST_229J_CURRENT_THEOREM_AUDIT_COMPLETE / PROVED_SANTENS_NONSPLIT_TORIC_BASE_MATCH_WITH_PHYSICAL_SUP_HEIGHT / PROVED_FIXED_FINITE_LOCAL_TEST_FUNCTION_FRAMEWORK_AVAILABLE_ON_X0 / PROVED_SELECTOR_SQUARECLASS_INDEPENDENCE / PROVED_GENERIC_SIMULTANEOUS_COVER_DEGREE_4 / NO_GROWING_SUPPORT_ERROR_OR_GEOMETRIC_SIEVE / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0


TYPE: POST-229J THEOREM DELTA / NONSPLIT TORIC HEIGHT-ZETA REMATCH / FIXED-FINITE LOCAL CONDITIONS / SIMULTANEOUS DOUBLE-COVER DEGREE CERTIFICATION


OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
PREVIOUS_POST_229_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229J
FOUNDATIONAL_INTERNAL_STRUCTURAL_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229F
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229J proved that the fixed reversed selector base
  X0: X^2+Y^2=Z^2,
      Z^2+T^2=S^2
has dense Q-torus
  T0 = Res^1_{Q(i)/Q} G_m x G_m,
that the toric minimal resolution Xtilde0 is defined over Q, and that
  -K_Xtilde0 = pi^* O_X0(1).
It also proved that on the primitive positive physical chart [X:Y:Z:T:S]=[x:y:z:e:R], the standard projective sup-height is exactly R.


The current task is not to extend the 229J identity chain. It is to rematch a concrete post-229J theorem input against the exact non-split Q-toric form and to certify the generic degree of the simultaneous selector cover.


2. Santens 2026 now applies to the non-split reversed base with the physical height


Tim Santens, “Manin's conjecture for integral points on toric varieties,” Proc. London Math. Soc. 133 (2026), e70203, first published 26 Aug 2026, DOI 10.1112/plms.70203, proves bounded-height asymptotics for smooth proper toric varieties over number fields without assuming that the relevant Neron-Severi torus is split. The paper explicitly notes that the universal-torsor method is used with nonsplit T_NS and that D=empty recovers a proof of Manin's conjecture for toric varieties.


Theorem 1.1 allows a height corresponding to a big divisor. On Xtilde0 take
  L = pi^* O_X0(1) = -K_Xtilde0.
This is big. Pull back the standard adelic sup metric from O_X0(1). On the positive physical dense-torus points this height is exactly
  H_L = max(x,y,z,e,R) = R,
by 229F/229J.


Therefore the previous 229J caveat “Batyrev–Tschinkel theorem species applies but an exact leading constant for the physical sup metric was not claimed” is no longer a height-applicability obstacle for this Santens theorem species: the physical sup metric itself is an admissible adelic height for the big line bundle L.


RESULT_229K_SANTENS_NONSPLIT_BASE_MATCH=PROVED.
RESULT_229K_PHYSICAL_SUP_HEIGHT_IS_ADMISSIBLE_SANTENS_HEIGHT=PROVED_ON_DENSE_PHYSICAL_TORUS.
RESULT_229K_BASE_SPLITNESS_AND_METRIC_BLOCKER=REMOVED_FOR_SANTENS_BASE_COUNT.


This is a result about the reversed toric base X0. It is NOT an identification of the exact Euler-brick M3 measure from LOCAL/225 with X0. The 229F reversal deliberately changes which square conditions define the base.


3. Fixed finite local test functions are available


Santens's height-zeta setup permits a finite set S of places at which the local factor f_v is prescribed; at finite places f_v is locally constant, and outside S it is the indicator of the chosen integral model. Thus fixed finite collections of p-adic residue neighbourhoods on the non-split toric base can be inserted into the same height-zeta framework.


Consequently, after 229J, the obstacle on the reversed X0 base is no longer “can a non-split toric asymptotic see fixed local congruence conditions at all?”. It can, for each fixed finite local support.


RESULT_229K_FIXED_FINITE_LOCAL_NEIGHBOURHOOD_COUNTING=AVAILABLE_ON_X0.


However the published theorem gives an asymptotic for each fixed test function/local support; it does not provide the Huang-style conductor-uniform effective error needed to let the set or modulus of local conditions grow with the height bound. No non-split Ekedahl/geometric-sieve theorem with the required growing-support uniformity is extracted from Santens.


RESULT_229K_GROWING_LOCAL_SUPPORT_UNIFORMITY=NOT_PROVED.
RESULT_229K_NONSPLIT_EFFECTIVE_GEOMETRIC_SIEVE=STILL_OPEN.


This distinction is load-bearing. A fixed finite set of local selector restrictions can change a leading constant, but Stage37 needs an absolute selector count strong enough against M3(B)>>B^(1/3), or an exact same-M3 receiver. An arbitrarily small fixed constant times a base count of order B polylog does not change the B-exponent. Letting the number of primes grow would require a uniform error/level-of-distribution theorem that is not present here.


4. The two selector squareclasses are geometrically independent; generic cover degree is exactly 4


229J gave on the split torus, after the degree-two isogeny p=uv, q=v/u, the squareclasses
  F_plus  = (1+p^2)(1+q^2),
  F_minus = (p^2-1)(q^2-1).


Work over Qbar(p,q). Consider the prime divisor p-i. Then
  ord_{p-i}(F_plus)=1,
  ord_{p-i}(F_minus)=0.
Hence F_plus is not a square and [F_plus] is nonzero in Qbar(p,q)^*/Qbar(p,q)^{*2}.


Consider the prime divisor p-1. Then
  ord_{p-1}(F_minus)=1,
  ord_{p-1}(F_plus)=0.
Hence F_minus is not a square.


If [F_plus]=[F_minus], then F_plus*F_minus would be a square; but at p-i its valuation is 1. Thus [F_plus] and [F_minus] are linearly independent over F_2.


Therefore
  [Qbar(p,q)(sqrt(F_plus),sqrt(F_minus)) : Qbar(p,q)] = 4.
The simultaneous double cover is generically degree 4 and geometrically integral on the dense torus. Since any squareclass dependence on the original Q-torus would persist after base change and pullback to the split torus, the original simultaneous selector cover is also generically degree 4.


RESULT_229K_SELECTOR_SQUARECLASS_INDEPENDENCE=PROVED.
RESULT_229K_SIMULTANEOUS_SELECTOR_GENERIC_DEGREE=4.
RESULT_229K_SIMULTANEOUS_SELECTOR_COVER_GEOMETRICALLY_INTEGRAL_ON_DENSE_OPEN=PROVED.


This upgrades the “most favorable possible generic degree d=4” grant in 229C from a preflight assumption to an exact structural fact for the 229J/229F selector cover. It does not improve the 229C height/exponent ceiling by itself.


5. Why this still does not reopen production


A. Geometry / reversed-base route:
Santens now supplies non-split base asymptotics and fixed-finite local test functions at the exact physical R-height. But no growing-prime uniform error, geometric sieve, or direct count of the global square-lift image is supplied.


B. Generic thin-set route:
The selector fiber product is now certified geometrically integral degree 4, but 229C already showed that even a favorable degree-4 affine thin-set black-box, under its then-available physical normalization, does not meet the Stage37 exponent budget. 229K removes the degree-certification caveat, not the height/counting firewall.


C. LOCAL route:
M3-LOCAL-GATE-001 is on the exact Euler-brick M3 measure. X0 is the 229F reversed toric base obtained by making the face+space chain the base and moving the other two face-square conditions into the cover. Santens counting on X0 therefore does not supply the fixed-Q twisted exact-M3 asymptotic requested by 225. LOCAL_REOPEN remains false.


D. PAIR/A/FIB:
No exact occupied-M3 weight, centered covariance, or moving-base second moment is produced. All remain held.


POST_229_REOPEN_TRIGGER_FOUND=false.
GEOMETRY_REOPEN=false.
LOCAL_REOPEN=false.
PAIR_REOPEN=false.
A_REOPEN=false.
FIB_REOPEN=false.
M3_T11_230=NOT_ISSUED.
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0.
P_OVER_M3_LIMIT_PROVED=false.
RESEARCH_PRODUCTION_STATUS=HOLD_PENDING_GENUINELY_NEW_THEOREM_INPUT.


6. Sharpened theorem watch after 229K


The geometry watch can now be stated more narrowly.


The missing theorem is NOT:
- non-split toric Manin/base counting;
- ability to impose a fixed finite set of local conditions;
- generic irreducibility/degree of the simultaneous selector cover.


Those pieces are now available/certified.


The missing theorem IS one of:


(A) NONSPLIT_TORIC_EFFECTIVE_LEVEL_OF_DISTRIBUTION:
an effective congruence/equidistribution theorem for Xtilde0 or its nonsplit universal torsor with error uniform in a growing finite modulus/local support, strong enough to run an Ekedahl/Hilbert sieve on the two selector squareclasses and obtain a B-exponent deficit, not only a logarithmic or fixed-constant loss;


(B) GAUSSIAN_NORM_TRIPLE_EXACT_HEIGHT_COUNT:
a direct count for p in Q(i) with N(p), N(p^2-1), N(p^2+1) rational squares, preserving the 229F physical R-height and primitive/canonical multiplicity, with an exponent meeting the Stage37 denominator target;


(C) FULL_FOUR_QUADRIC_SOURCE_COUNT:
a theorem for the actual special four-quadric physical surface in seven projective coordinates, exploiting its special structure and exact R-height strongly enough to beat the existing B^(1/2+epsilon) endpoint bound / Stage37 threshold.


Do not start another identity-only continuation from the degree-4 certification. The next legal geometry move is a theorem with quantitative growing-support or exact-height saving.


7. Sources checked


- Tim Santens, “Manin's conjecture for integral points on toric varieties,” Proc. London Math. Soc. 133 (2026), e70203, DOI 10.1112/plms.70203. Relevant points: arbitrary smooth proper toric variety over a number field; nonsplit Neron-Severi torus handled; big-divisor heights; D=empty recovers rational toric Manin; local factors f_v in the height-zeta setup are locally constant at finite places and unrestricted at a fixed finite set of places.
- Zhizhong Huang, “Equidistribution of rational points and the geometric sieve for toric varieties,” arXiv:2111.01509v3. Effective congruence/geometric-sieve mechanism remains split-toric over Q.
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229J.
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229F.
- Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229C.
- M3-T11-225.


AUDIT SCOPE


This is a post-229J theorem-applicability audit plus an exact function-field squareclass proof. It is not an independent hostile audit of cards 186–229. It claims no perfect-cuboid existence/nonexistence result and no global counting credit.

Card parent=M3-Research-Cards; card content present; MAIN latest delta=229K and card pointer present; active ROUTE 229K result block present; current LEDGER 229K change record present; CARD-INDEX row475 and 案内 latest/read-order updated. ﻿Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229J — exact non-split Q-toric descent and Gaussian norm-selector normal form


STATUS: POST_229I_STRUCTURAL_THEOREM_AUDIT_COMPLETE / PROVED_X0_IS_NON_SPLIT_Q_TORIC / PROVED_DENSE_TORUS_RES1_QI_Q_TIMES_GM / PROVED_GAUSSIAN_ONE_VARIABLE_SELECTOR_NORMAL_FORM / PROVED_BASE_SPLITNESS_BLOCKER_REMOVED_AT_TORIC_THEOREM_LEVEL / EFFECTIVE_THIN_COVER_COUNT_STILL_OPEN / NO_REOPEN / GLOBAL_CREDIT=0
TYPE: POST-229I GEOMETRY/THEOREM DELTA AUDIT / NON-SPLIT TORIC DESCENT / SIMULTANEOUS KUMMER NORMAL FORM
OPERATIONAL_AUTHORITY: M3-T11-229
LATEST_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTRUCTION: M3-T11-228
FOUNDATIONAL_INTERNAL_STRUCTURAL_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229F
PREVIOUS_EXTERNAL_THEOREM_DELTA: Stage37-NEW-INPUT-DELTA-AUDIT-229I
PRIMARY_GATE: M3-T11-GATE-001 OPEN
M3_T11_230: NOT ISSUED
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT: 0


1. Scope


229F fixed the coefficient-free selector base
  X0: X^2+Y^2=Z^2,
      Z^2+T^2=S^2
inside P^4, proved geometric type 4A1 quartic del Pezzo, and proved that on the primitive positive physical chart the standard projective sup-height is exactly the physical height R.


229F correctly warned that the displayed Q-form is not split: it has two rational nodes and one conjugate pair over Q(i). The current task is to determine whether this Q-form is nevertheless a toric compactification over Q, and whether modern toric counting/sieve theorems then meet the simultaneous-cover contract.


2. Exact Q-toric descent of X0


Work on the dense open Z != 0 and set K=Q(i). Define
  u=(X+iY)/Z,
  v=(S+T)/Z.


The first quadric gives
  u * conjugate(u) = (X^2+Y^2)/Z^2 = 1,
so u is a point of the norm-one torus Res^1_{K/Q} G_m.


The second quadric gives
  ((S+T)/Z)*((S-T)/Z)=1,
hence v is in G_m and
  (S-T)/Z=v^(-1).


Conversely, from any
  u in Res^1_{K/Q} G_m,
  v in G_m,
one recovers
  X/Z=(u+u^(-1))/2,
  Y/Z=(u-u^(-1))/(2i),
  S/Z=(v+v^(-1))/2,
  T/Z=(v-v^(-1))/2.


Therefore
  X0 intersect {Z != 0}
is Q-isomorphic to the two-dimensional algebraic torus

5. Exact simultaneous selector normal form on the split torus


Use the physical identification from 229F:
  [X:Y:Z:T:S]=[x:y:z:e:R].
The two remaining face-square conditions are
  U^2=T^2+X^2,
  V^2=T^2+Y^2.

  X=(u+u^(-1))/2,
  Y=(u-u^(-1))/(2i),
  T=(v-v^(-1))/2.


A direct calculation gives
  4(T^2+X^2)

  4(T^2+Y^2)
